O LORD, DO NOT REBUKE ME IN YOUR FURY, NOR CHASTEN ME IN YOUR WRATH. Lord, do not reproach me in your hot anger.
for that I wait. And my substance is before you. Therefore my being is before you. That I am Jeduthun pleases you; that is in your sight.
If I have substance of gold and silver, even men can see that. From all my iniquities deliver me. Release me from all my unrighteousness.
What need does Jeduthun have of this prayer? Only that he teaches us to be humble, even though we have become aware of grace in ourselves.
You have made me a reproach to the foolish. You have made me a reproach to the foolish man. You wanted me to be among them,
and to tell the truth to those who love vanity more, and to whom I am nothing but a mockery. I was mute and did not open my mouth, because you did it.
Among such people I became mute, and I did not open my mouth, because you did it. You gave me the patience
to be able to keep silent so profitably. Remove your strokes from me, for I have fainted from the strength of your hand in rebukes.
Take your chastisements away from me, for I am weary from the rebukes of your mighty hand. Spare me after so many scourgings
that have made me powerless. For iniquity you have corrected man. Because of unrighteousness you chastise man.
You hold his guilt against him. And you made his soul waste away like a spider. And you made him waste away and wither
like the spider. You made him so worn down by hardships and so lean, as the spider is in its limbs.
In this way you punished him for his unrighteousness. Nevertheless every man is troubled in vain.
Every man is nonetheless troubled in mind over vain things. For all this he does not give up idle worries,
sometimes about clothing, sometimes about food. What he worries about depends on God, not on himself;
therefore his worries are idle. Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication; with your ears perceive my tears.
Hear my prayer and my supplication, Lord; with your ears perceive my tears. Perceive what they ask for,
why I shed them. Do not be silent, for I am a stranger with you, and a pilgrim, as all my fathers were.
Do not be silent: do not fail to say, "Your sins are forgiven you," or "I am your salvation." For I am a newcomer with you, and an exile,
as all my forefathers were. They all came from Babylon to Jerusalem and were pilgrims here. As Paul says:
"As long as we are in the body, we are pilgrims away from the Lord." Forgive me, that I may be refreshed. Forgive me my sins; unburden me of them,
that I may be cooled from my worries and find rest in my conscience. Before I go away and shall be no more.
Before I go hence and am here no longer. Or it means: before I go hence in such a way that I no longer exist.
For whoever is not with God does not exist. His existence is of no use to him; therefore he does not exist. Here praise the Lord, for the psalm is good.
UNTO THE END, A PSALM OF DAVID. WAITING I WAITED FOR THE LORD. The Church says: Waiting I waited for my Lord. We wait with waiting
for what we greatly long for; that is the reason for this doubling. And he attended to me. And he looked toward me. That is, he took notice of me.
[that] you now want a contrite and humbled heart. Then I said: Behold, I come. Then I said: Lo, I come.
When I commanded that an unblemished lamb be offered, then I meant myself. Then I promised what I have now done:
that I myself would come and become the sacrificial victim. At the head of the book it is written of me that I should do your will.
In the first scroll it is written of me that I do your will, as it says: His will is in the law of the Lord.
My God, I willed it. My God, I willed what was promised there, and I have shown that will.
And your law in the midst of my heart. And I willed your law in the midst of my heart, as it also says there:
He will meditate on his law day and night. I have proclaimed your righteousness in the great church. I proclaimed your righteousness in the catholic Church.
In that I did your will. Behold, I will not restrain my lips; Lord, you know it. Behold,
I do not close my lips so as not to speak your righteousness. You know that in my heart,
where no human knows it. Here Christ teaches us that his righteousness should be in our mind, not only in our mouth.
I have not hidden your righteousness in my heart. I did not hide your righteousness in my heart. When it was time for it,
I did not conceal it. But in the Passion it was not the time for it, so I kept silent. I have spoken of your truth and your salvation.
I declared your truth and your Saviour. I revealed to them that I am Christ. I have not hidden your mercy and your truth from the great assembly.
I did not hide your grace or your truth before the great multitude. By grace I mean this: whoever renounces his sins,
you forgive them to him. And by truth I mean this: to whoever walks in righteousness [?], you give the crown.
But you, Lord, do not put your mercies far from me; your mercy and your truth have always upheld me. But do not put far from me
your grace. Do not withdraw your grace from my imperfect members, which still limp in righteousness,
for your grace and your truth have always received me. Love comes from grace, fear from truth.
These received me and lead me. For evils without number have surrounded me. That is why there is need, I mean,
that you not put your mercies far from me: because countless evils have surrounded me in those members. Listen to what they are.
My iniquities have seized me. My iniquities have caught me. There are so many of them that they cannot be numbered.
And I was not able to see. And because of how many they were, I was not able to see the true light,
which is God himself. They are multiplied beyond the hairs of my head. They are more
than the hairs of my head. Such a multitude can easily choke a person who does not guard against them. Whoever does not commit grave sins
but does not fear many small ones is buried by sand, even though no great mass crushes him.
And my heart has forsaken me. And my heart has forsaken me. That is: it is unable to know itself.
Just as Peter did not know his own heart when he said: "I am ready to die with you." What wonder is it if God forsakes the heart
that forsakes itself? Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me. Since that is so, may it now please you, Lord,
to deliver me. O Lord, look to helping me. Lord, look to my help; that is, be ready to help me.
Let them be confounded and put to shame together who seek my soul to take it away. Let them be ashamed together because of my miracles,
and let them be afraid because of my resurrection, those who seek my soul to kill it.
Let them be turned backward and blush who think evil against me. Let them be turned around behind me, so that they follow after me,
and let them be ashamed who wish me evil. Let them straightaway bear their confusion who say to me, "Well done, well done." Let them straightaway bear their shame,
those who say to me "Well done, well done," and do it mockingly, or speak it to me as praise,
as if it came from me and not from God. Let them exult and rejoice who seek you, O Lord. Let them leap for joy and rejoice,
those who seek you, Lord, and say "Well done" to you, because it is you who give it. And let them say always: The Lord be magnified,
those who love your salvation. And let those who love your Savior say always: May the Lord be magnified,
for he gives to man everything good that he has. But I am needy and poor; the Lord takes care of me. But I, to whom they say
"Well done, well done": I am needy and poor! God takes care of me; in him I am rich.
Be my helper and my protector, O Lord; do not delay. Be my helper and protector, Lord my God; do not delay.
Unto the end, for David himself. Blessed is he who understands concerning the needy and the poor. Blessed, says the prophet, is he
who has understanding concerning the needy and the poor. That person understands Christ who understands why he became needy and poor:
so that he might make us rich. He said of himself in the preceding psalm: But I am a beggar and poor,
and the Lord takes care of me. How does it appear that he is blessed? In the evil day the Lord will deliver him. On the day of judgment God will deliver him.
What helps him is this: he did not take offence at him, nor misunderstand him, and he knew him inwardly as God, even though he saw him outwardly as a man.
May the Lord preserve him and give him life. May God keep him safe in all the perils of the world and make him alive, for all others are dead
except those who live in him. And may he make him blessed on earth. And may he make him blessed in the homeland of the saints.
And may he not deliver him into the hands of his enemies. And may he not give him into the power of his enemies, neither here nor in eternity.
May the Lord bring him help upon the bed of his sorrow. May God bring him help upon the bed of his pain.
His weakness is called the bed of sorrow. I mean someone who cannot get up because of weakness.
if he cannot bridle the flesh, then may God help him. You have turned all his bed in his sickness.
You have turned all his bed into his sickness. Where he wanted to rest, you gave him unrest.
If he hurried to gain house and household, wife and property and other possessions, you made him hold all of it with bitterness.
Why? So that he would love nothing else but eternal life. On the bed of pain you help him; on the bed of rest you are against him.
That is how you train your own. I said: Lord, have mercy on me. Therefore I said: Lord, have mercy on me.
Heal my soul, for I have sinned against you. Heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.
If you did not spare Christ, your Son, though he was guiltless, I, however, am guilty.
You rightly scourge me so that you may heal me, because when I was whole in paradise, I did not listen to you.
My enemies spoke evil to me. My enemies, says Christ, spoke ill of me. What did they say? When will he die
and his name perish? When will he die, and when will his name be destroyed? They said: This is the heir.
Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours. And they came in to see. And they came in to me
to spy on me. Judas spied on me myself; my other members are spied on by many.
Their heart spoke vanity. Their heart spoke what was worthless. They intended to lie against me. They gathered iniquity to themselves.
They gathered iniquity to themselves. They thought they were harming me; they harmed themselves. They went outside and spoke to the same end,
that is, with one counsel. Those who had gone in there went out and spoke with one voice.
With one voice they plotted my death. And all my enemies whispered against me. All my enemies went about whispering against me.
Against me they plotted evil for me. Against me they thought evil for me. They devised death for me; that became life for others.
They set an unjust word against me. They set an unjust word against me. That is: He is guilty of death. Shall he who sleeps
not rise again? Do you think that he who now sleeps will not rise afterward? You think you have
killed him, but he is sleeping. Death is sleep to him, because he lets himself into it for a while
and then soon throws it off again. The man of my peace, in whom I hoped, who ate my bread, has greatly increased his tripping-up of me.
Judas, my protégé (that is, the one who kissed me), in whom I trusted, that is, in whom my followers trusted,
who ate with me, tripped me up far and wide. Far and wide because he drew the Jews into it.
If you would rather say: he magnified his tripping-up of me by being against me, that is still the same thing.
But you, Lord, have mercy on me. But you have mercy on me, Lord. This is spoken in the form of a servant, and in the form of the needy and the poor.
That is to say: I directed my thought above the sight of myself. Inwardly I see myself.
Understanding, which is given to the sons of Korah, shows me my invisible soul, and far above it my invisible God.
For it is changeable; he is unchangeable. If it could not reach above itself, how then would it reach him
who is so high above it? "For I shall go into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God." So I learned to seek him.
For I came into the place of the wonderful tabernacles, wonderful here on earth, until one arrives fully
up to the house of God. Outside the Church one need not seek him.
The Church is wonderful in all God's faithful, wonderful for many virtues. In it one must go on until one fully arrives there,
where God's house is, where wondering ceases, because the fountain of understanding is there, and all questions are untied there.
"With the voice of exultation and confession, the sound of one feasting." Within it, in the voice of joy and confession, I hear the sound of one feasting.
My soul feasts on these two voices: that I praise God, and that I know myself, until I come there.
They sound so sweet to me that their sound is a feast to me. "Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me?"
Why are you sad, and why do you make me joyless, my soul? As if you did not know how to answer those
who say to you, "Where is your God?" As if you were not in the wonderful tabernacle, at those feasts of exultation and confession.
Why do these people who wander in error in this world trouble you? Why do they grieve you so? "Hope in God."
Hold fast to God, put your hope in him; he will take you out of there. "For I will confess to him."
He will do so, because I confess to him. What do I confess? "The salvation of my countenance, my God." The salvation of my face is my God.
This I confess to him: he heals my face, which is sad now, and makes it glad when I see him.
"My soul is troubled within myself." Turned toward myself, my soul is saddened; turned toward God, it is comforted. He is steadfast;
I am unsteadfast. My unsteadfastness weighs on me; his steadfastness gives me courage. It gives me hope of coming there
where I shall become steadfast. "Therefore I will remember you from the land of the Jordan and of Hermon, from the little mountain." Therefore I remember you from the land of the Jordan
and from Hermon, the little mountain. In Latin, Jordan means "their descent" and Hermon means "anathema". The Jordan signifies baptism;
anathema signifies abomination. In both of them humility is understood. Humility teaches a person to lower himself, which is called "to descend",
and to loathe himself, which is called "to anathematize". So it means: being humble and making myself small,
I remember you. "Deep calls to deep." Abyss calls on abyss. The Old Testament foreshadows the New Testament.
"In the voice of your cataracts." In the voice of your waterfalls, that is to say:
In God we shall be praised all the day. In God we shall be praised every day. Where there is day without night, there we shall be praised.
For you have rescued us from those who afflict us. And in your name they shall give praise forever. And in your name we shall give praise forever.
In that world the praise of the saints is eternal, and they can never grow weary of it, for it is their blessedness. But now you have cast us off and put us to shame.
Although that is to come for us in eternity, you have nevertheless now thrust us away, your martyrs,
and put us to shame, because we who are called Christians are made hateful by the pagans. And you will not go out, O God, with our forces.
And you do not go out with us, God, among our forces, as you did before. You leave us powerless
when we rise up to march against our enemies, though you made our forefathers strong in battle.
You have turned us back before our enemies, that is, in front of our enemies. You have turned us away, turned our backs
before our enemies. You have scorned us while they looked on. And those who hated us plundered for themselves.
And those who hate us have carried us off for themselves. You have given us like sheep for food, and scattered us among the nations.
You have given us to them to be devoured like lambs for slaughter, and you have scattered us among the heathen.
Because this is the voice of the martyrs, this lament is to be understood of those who fell away during martyrdom
and turned back to paganism. You sold your people without price. You gave away your people without receiving others in exchange for them.
You gave your martyrs up to slaughter. What did you receive in return for them? And there was no multitude in their exchanges.
And there was no great payment in the bargain. Of those who were given away there were many;
of those received in return there were none. You have made us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a mockery to those who are around us.
You have made us a reproach to our neighbours, and an object of scorn and mockery to those placed around us.
You have made us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples. For the heathen you have made us a likeness of your passion,
and a [?head-]wagging for the people, as you were for the Jews. All the day my shame is before me. All day long my shame was before me.
Other people feel ashamed now and then; our shame went on and on. And the confusion of my face has covered me. And the shame of my face
covered me. Because of the voice of the one who reproaches and reviles, before the face of the enemy and the persecutor. Where did it come from?
From the voice of the one who reproaches and speaks against me, and from the sight of the enemy
and of the persecutor, who is always present against me. All these things have come upon us. All this has come upon us
For understanding, for the sons of Korah. So that they may know how God led our forefathers out of Egypt,
and how he will lead us in the resurrection out of this Egypt of this world, so that in the meantime we must suffer every hardship here.
and [that] we are to be tested to see whether we are willing to serve God gratis, that is, without payment. Freely he gave us life,
freely he redeemed us, freely we ought to serve him. I mean that we should desire no reward here,
but in the future. Therefore it says after this: "Nor have we forgotten you." Nor did we forget you because of that.
No tribulation made us forget you, because you willed it to happen to us. "For understanding, for the sons of Korah": for us sons of Korah,
for us sons of the cross. "And we have not acted wickedly in your covenant." Nor did we do wrong in what you appointed for us,
that is, in your law. "And our heart has not turned back." Nor did our heart give way backward, as the hearts of those do
who come to despair because of hardships. "And you have turned our paths aside from your way." And you turned our paths away from your way.
That is, you taught us how far our way, which we wanted to go, is from yours,
which you want us to go. Ours leads to death; yours leads to life. "For you have humbled us in the place of affliction."
For you have humbled us in this wretched place, in this toilsome
world. "And the shadow of death has covered us." And the image of death has covered us. What is that? Nothing but mortality, which is common to all.
But what is death itself? Nothing but eternal damnation with the devil. "If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have spread out our hands to a strange god,
will not God search this out?" If we had forgotten the name of our God, and if we had spread out our hands to a strange god,
would God not ask about it? Why does he ask about what he already knows? Only so that he may let us know it,
and so that we, by recognizing ourselves, may be made better. "For he knows the secrets of the heart." He knows the secrets of the heart.
Therefore he has no need to ask. Yet he asks when he tests us, and through the testing he makes us recognize who we are.
So he did with Peter, who did not know himself before the temptation, when he said: "With you I am ready to die,"
but who began to know himself in the temptation, when he wept over his denial. "For your sake we are put to death all day long."
You know the secrets of our hearts: that we are put to death for your sake all day long, that is, at all times,
not for vainglory, nor for our crimes. If there were none who would readily die out of boastfulness,
not out of love, then Paul would not have said: "If I give my body to be burned, but have not love,
it profits me nothing." "We are counted as sheep for the slaughter." And [you know] that we are reckoned as sheep for sacrifice.
Sheep do not defend themselves; we do not defend ourselves. "Arise, why do you sleep, O Lord?" Stand up, Lord, why do you sleep?
This is an abuse of a word, that is, a misuse of a word, which in Greek is called catachresis. How can God sleep?
Rather, his martyrs cry out to Christ that he make his resurrection known to the gentiles, for he sleeps to those who know him as dead.
Therefore God, your God, has anointed you. Therefore God anointed you, your God. The Father consecrated you and anointed you,
because you loved right and hated wrong. What is the ointment? It is spiritual and invisible, which by something bodily and visible
is signified. With the oil of gladness above your fellows. With the oil of joy he anointed you; that is innocence,
which remembers nothing of anything that might weigh on it, so that it would need to repent. Above your fellows (or: partners). That is to say,
further than other saints, because from you, the anointed one, others are called anointed. Myrrh and gutta and cassia from your garments.
From your garment come the scents of myrrh, and of gutta, which is called ammoniac, and of cassia, which is called fistula.
That is to say: from the faithful and from the whole Church comes the report of virtues, which is as sweet as the scent of precious
herbs. Out of the ivory houses. It comes out of ivory houses, that is,
from holy virgins, who are signified by ivory, because the elephant is a chaste animal
and, beyond one mate, takes no other. From which, that is, among which, the daughters of kings have delighted you in your honor.
Among those houses the daughters of kings, who were born to your honor, delighted you. Those who delighted you
were the daughters of the apostles, chosen for your honor, not for theirs, because they are called Christians, not Petrians or Paulians.
Or the daughters of kings are the many churches, which are all called Christ's, not Peter's or Paul's. The queen stood at your right hand.
The queen herself, your Church, which is made up of many churches, stood at your right hand.
There her children hear: 'Come, you blessed of my Father.' She who stands at the left is not the queen;
she hears: 'Go into the eternal fire.' In gilded clothing. In a gilded garment, that is, with the adornment of wisdom.
Surrounded with variety. Wrapped around with many colors, of either virtues or languages,
because she exists in various languages and she has various virtues. Hear, daughter, and see. 'Hear, daughter, and see,' says the prophet.
Mother of many children, daughter of the prophets and apostles, [hear] what the gospel of Christ commands you, and after that you will see the glory of God.
Faith in the gospel cleanses your heart, so that you can see him whom only the pure in heart shall see. And incline your ear.
And humbly incline your ear; take careful note of this counsel. And forget your people and your father's house.
And put out of mind your people, the people of Babylon, from whom you were born, and your father's house, the devil's, who is king there,
who bore you unsightly, with the stains of your sins; and you are reborn in Christ to the beauty of innocence.
For the king has desired your beauty. For the king, your bridegroom, desires your beauty. He is beautiful through himself;
you become beautiful through him. He wants you to be without spot and without wrinkle. He makes you so.
And the meditation of my heart [shall speak] prudence. So the thinking of my heart speaks wisdom. From the heart came my words,
with which I make you wise. I do not act like those who say one thing and want another. I will incline my ear to a parable.
I incline my ear to my saying. I myself do what I teach. But the Pharisees teach
what they do not carry out in deed. I will open my proposition on the psaltery. Through the body I open my secret. I myself come in the body (in corpore)
and teach you a hard understanding. Why shall I fear in the evil day? Why should I be afraid on the evil day,
when the day of death comes? Shall the iniquity of my heel surround me? Will the injustice of my heel then surround me,
that is, of my end, as it does others? Those who trust in their own strength and glory in the multitude of their riches?
As it does those who trust in their own strength and pride themselves on their great
riches? A brother does not redeem; shall a man redeem? Whoever says "Father" to God says "brother" to Christ. The one whom Christ did not redeem,
can a man redeem him, as those suppose who rely on their own strength? He shall not give to God his propitiation. Whoever supposes this
does not give God anything with which to win His favour. And the price of the redemption of his soul. Nor the price of his soul's ransom.
He does not give alms; he does not make himself friends of the mammon of iniquity. And he shall labour forever, and shall still live unto the end.
And because of this he is always in torment, and lives on forever without end. Just as the rich man, buried in hell, lives without end in torment.
He shall not see destruction when he sees the wise dying. Such a person does not recognize destruction when he sees wise men die,
and he says: "They are lost. What good has their wisdom done them?" If he recognized destruction,
he would know that he himself was lost, not they. The unwise and the foolish shall perish together. Those who are wise are not lost;
the unwise and the fool are lost together. The one who is so unwise that he does not know himself, and the one so foolish
that he does not care for his salvation: each of them is lost. And they shall leave their riches to strangers.
And they leave their riches to strangers. But what if they have children? Those too are strangers to them,
because they are of no use to them. Just as those who took possession of the rich man's wealth were strangers to him when he was in hell.
And their graves are their houses forever. And their graves, so they think, are their houses forever.
Their tents in generation and generation. And their tents from generation to generation. That is why they make marble tombs,
as if these were to be their dwellings forever. If the rich man had been housed there, he would not be burning in hell. They have called their
names in their lands, that is, in their graves. There at their graves they called on them by name.
Their descendants visited their graves and, holding feasts there, called on them there, according to heathen custom.
A psalm of Asaph. Who was Asaph? He was the son of Barachiel, one of the chief singers, of whom one reads in Paralipomenon [Chronicles],
who in those times sang these psalms to God. In that sense this psalm is Asaph's,
because he sang what David taught him. And to understand it more deeply: Asaph means "synagogue." The synagogue of the believers
and of the holy forefathers speaks here. This psalm is theirs. THE GOD OF GODS, THE LORD, HAS SPOKEN. The God of gods,
that is, of the saints, who are called gods by grace, the Lord himself, he spoke. What did he do by speaking?
And he called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting. He spoke and directed the whole earth to his faith, all who dwell on the earth,
from the rising of the sun to its setting. Out of Zion the beauty of his comeliness. From Zion comes his beautiful image.
Zion is in Jerusalem. From there came the apostles, who proclaimed Christ to us, whom his divinity adorned above all others.
God will come openly. God comes openly. He who came secretly before comes openly the second time. When he came,
he was judged; when he comes again, he will judge. Our God, and he will not keep silent. Our God comes
and does not keep silent, though he keeps silent now, for at the judgment he will say: GO INTO THE ETERNAL FIRE. A fire will burn before him.
Fire burns before him. It burns the chaff. Whoever recognizes himself as chaff, let him fear the fire. And round about him a mighty tempest.
And around him a strong wind. It separates the good from the evil. That wind is made by the winnowing fan that is in his hand,
as it says: WHOSE WINNOWING FAN IS IN HIS HAND, AND HE WILL CLEANSE HIS THRESHING FLOOR AND GATHER THE WHEAT INTO HIS BARN,
BUT THE CHAFF HE WILL BURN WITH UNQUENCHABLE FIRE. He shall call the heaven above, and the earth. He summons the heaven above, and
the earth. That is, he summons the righteous and the unrighteous to his judgment. Why? To separate his people. To separate his people.
From whom? From the wicked. Though the wicked and the good dwell together here, there he will separate them.
Gather his saints to him. The synagogue now speaks to the angels. Gather his saints to him. For then it will happen as CHRIST says in the Gospel:
FOR HE WILL SEND HIS ANGELS, AND ALL NATIONS WILL BE GATHERED BEFORE HIM. Who set his testament in order. Who set his testament in order.
Those who distribute and act as he has commanded in the books. Those who show charity, give alms,
and receive guests. Above sacrifices. Such works are dearer to God than offerings. For he said: I DESIRE MERCY
AND NOT SACRIFICE. And the heavens will declare his justice, for God is judge. And by doing this the heavens proclaim,
that is, the righteous proclaim, his justice, for they know that God himself is the judge, whom nothing deceives.
Hear, my people, and I will speak. Now CHRIST speaks. Hear, my people, and then I will speak. If you will not listen to me,
then you are not my people, and I will keep silent. Israel, and I will testify to you. Hear, Israel, and I will tell you.
"And cleanse me from my offense." And cleanse me of my misdeed. "For I acknowledge my iniquity." For I myself acknowledge my wrongdoing.
Therefore do not take note of it yourself. Because I punish it, therefore do not punish it yourself. "And my offense is ever before me."
And my misdeed is always before me. I keep remembering, always, what I have done.
"Against you alone have I sinned." Against you alone I sinned. You alone are a just judge who repays, because you alone are without sin. Or else it means this:
If another man sins, he sins against God alone; if a king sins, he sins against God and the king [?]. "And I have done evil before you."
And I did evil before you. It grieves me that I dared to do this while you were looking on.
"That you may be justified in your words." Have mercy on me, so that you may be true in your words. Which words?
"Of the fruit of your body I will set upon your throne." "And that you may prevail when you are judged": namely, that you must do nothing unworthy.
And you prevail in upholding your promise when you are judged as to whether you could rightly abandon it [?].
If someone should say that I have forfeited it, then remember your mercy and set it right [?]. "For behold, I was conceived in iniquities,"
"and in sins my mother bore me." Behold, I was conceived in wrongdoing, and my mother bore me in sins.
Have mercy on me, for besides new guilt I have old guilt, with which I was conceived and born.
Which is that? It is the guilt that came from Adam to all people, and baptism was instituted because of it.
Christ alone came here without it. "For behold, you have loved truth." Behold, you loved the truth.
It pleased you that I told the truth in confessing my sins, as it says: "A pure confession frees from death." "The uncertain and hidden things
of your wisdom you have made known to me." You revealed to me the uncertain and hidden things of your wisdom.
You showed me that Christ, your wisdom, was to come here into the world, even though I have now gone so far astray.
"You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed." When he comes, you will sprinkle me with hyssop, as lepers are sprinkled, and then I shall be cleansed.
For it is commanded in Leviticus that lepers were to be sprinkled seven times with hyssop dipped in the blood of the sacrifice,
and that they were healed by this. "You will wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow." Then you will wash me, and then I shall be whiter than snow.
For you will give me a soul purer than any body could become. "To my hearing you will give joy and gladness."
You will let me hear joy and gladness when you say: "Come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom
that has been prepared for you from the beginning of the world." "And the humbled bones shall rejoice." And then they will rejoice,
the bones that are now humbled in penitence. There is also another kind of hearing that gladdens a person, one that is in the heart. John spoke of it:
"The friend of the bridegroom stands and hears him, and rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom's voice." A hearing of this kind makes the bones humbled.
because he recognizes the glory of the one whose voice he has heard inwardly. The prophets and apostles and all the teachers had this inward hearing.
From this, this sentence can also be understood: Turn away your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.
Turn your gaze away from my sins, and blot out all my sins. Create a clean heart in me, O God. Create
a clean heart in me, so clean that I do not do wrong like this again. And renew a right spirit within my inward parts.
And a right mind, by which I mean reason, which I made crooked by sinning: renew it in my inmost parts,
from which this adultery came. Strengthen me there, where I was just now frail. Do not cast me away from your face.
Do not cast me away from your sight. Cleanse me so that I may see you.
And do not take your holy spirit from me. And do not take your holy spirit from me, that is, the spirit of prophecy,
which I had before, however much I have now forfeited it. Restore to me the joy of your salvation.
Give me back the joy of your Savior, Christ, which I had before these sins, and which I now see has been diminished in me.
And strengthen me with the principal spirit. And strengthen me with the foremost spirit. Who is that, if not God, of whom it is written:
GOD IS SPIRIT. Strengthen me in this way: since you have now forgiven me, let me not become guilty again.
I will teach the wicked your ways. Then I will teach the unrighteous your ways, and tell them how you showed mercy to me, a wicked man,
so that they too do not despair of mercy. And the impious shall be converted to you. And the godless will be turned to you.
Not only to the unrighteous and sinful, but even to the very worst, I will then promise mercy from you,
if they are willing to mend their ways. Deliver me from blood, O God, God of my salvation. Deliver me, God, from the works of flesh and blood,
that is, of corruption, for it is written: FLESH AND BLOOD SHALL NOT POSSESS THE KINGDOM OF GOD, NOR SHALL CORRUPTION POSSESS INCORRUPTION.
Deliver me, God of my salvation, the salvation we do not yet have, because it is still to come.
And my tongue shall exult in your justice. And then my tongue will joyfully tell of your justice,
how you choose to receive the penitent not only out of mercy but also out of justice.
Lord, you will open my lips, and my mouth shall proclaim your praise. Lord, you open my lips,
and my mouth proclaims your praise: that you created me and did not abandon me when I sinned, and received my confession,
and released me from my sins. For if you had wanted sacrifice, I would surely have given it. For if you wanted an offering for my sins,
I would give it to you. I could bring you many young sacrificial animals, if you wanted them. But you will not delight in burnt offerings.
But you do not care for them; you do not want burnt offerings. They foreshadow the saving sacrifice, which will come when its time comes.
With what boldness is it said here: JUDGE ME? Except that he said before: SAVE ME. As if he said: BY SAV-
-ING, JUDGE ME. O God, hear my prayer. God, hear my prayer, for I do not wait for the flower of the Ziphites. Give ear to the words of my mouth.
Take in with your ears the words of my mouth, for I desire to receive eternal goods. May the prayer come to fulfillment
and not turn away from your ears. For strangers have risen up against me. For strangers have risen up
against me. Why strangers? Are the Ziphites not of the tribe of Judah, as David is? Only in that they are wicked, and therefore strangers.
And the strong have sought my soul. And strong men sought my soul. Saul and his servants plotted against my life.
And they have not set God before their sight. And they did not set God before their eyes. That is to say,
they did not have God before their eyes. For his sake they did not leave off from it. For behold, God helps me. See now, God helps me,
inwardly, in secret, not outwardly. And the Lord is the upholder of my soul. And the Lord is the receiver
of my soul. There is his help. Turn back the evils upon my enemies. Turn evil away from me, onto my enemies.
That is not a curse but a prophecy of the fire to come. In your truth destroy them. In your truth destroy them.
They flourish now in their vanity; let them then perish in your truth. Willingly will I sacrifice to you.
Willingly I make offering to you. Willingly I praise you, not for the sake of anything else, but for your own sake. And I will confess to your name, for it is good.
And I confess to your name, for it is good. It is nothing other than good. You are called Good; that is your name.
For you have delivered me out of every tribulation. For that you released me from all afflictions, that has taught me
that your name is good, and the highest good. And my eye has looked down upon my enemies. And my eye looked down upon my enemies,
the Ziphites. I have looked past their flower by looking upon you, and have learned this: that all flesh is grass, and the glory of man is like the flower of grass.
UNTO THE END, IN HYMNS, UNDERSTANDING, FOR DAVID HIMSELF. Christ is the end. Christ is our perfection. Toward him looks
what is sung in these praises. These same praises are understanding for David, that is, for the Christian people. Why are they understanding for him?
Because here is not a region of rejoicing but of groaning, not of exulting but of lamenting. And if there is any exultation in our hearts,
it is in hope, in hope, not in reality. HEAR, O GOD, MY PRAYER, AND DO NOT DESPISE MY SUPPLICATION.
Hear, God, my plea, and do not disregard my entreaty. Attend to me and hear me. Pay heed to me
and hear me. I am saddened in my exercise. I have become unhappy in my exercising. That is to say, in the suffering
that has come upon me from the wicked, which exercises and chastens me, I am so overcome that I can scarcely bear it.
And I am troubled by the voice of the enemy and by the affliction of the sinner. And I am troubled before the voice of the enemy.
I would surely have borne it. For if my enemy had spoken evil to me, I would have endured that. And if he who hated me had spoken great things against me,
I would surely have hidden myself from him. And if he who openly hates me had spoken arrogantly about me and had made threats against me,
then I would hide myself from him. I would give way to such people and go into the wilderness. But you, a man of one mind with me,
my guide and my acquaintance. But you, my like-minded one, my guide, my acquaintance, attacked me.
That weighs more heavily on me. You who took sweet food together with me. You ate together with me. We walked in the house of God in agreement.
You and I walked together in unity in the house of God. We confessed one God and prayed to one God,
whom you did not honour in me. Let death come upon them. Let death come upon those who are like this,
as fire took those who strove against Moses. And let them go down alive into hell. And let their leaders go alive to hell,
like Dathan and Abiram, who were the heads of the schism. But in the mystical sense, those go alive to hell
who are lost knowingly. For wickedness is in their dwellings. For malice is in their dwellings.
There, where they are to be only for a while, they show their wickedness. In the midst of them. In their midst. That is, their heart.
There is their malice. But I cried to God, and the Lord will save me. I, the Christian people, cried to God, and he saved me
and took me out from among the hostile. Evening and morning and noon I will tell and proclaim, and he will hear my voice.
In the evening [?], because Christ was then on the cross; in the morning, when Christ rose; at midday, when he was exalted
to the right hand of the Father, I tell and proclaim, and he hears my voice. He will redeem my soul in peace from those who draw near to me.
Though they storm against me, he redeems me in peace from those who draw near to me.
Why do you say "draw near"? For they were with me among many. For they were with me among the many who are chaff,
not with the few who are wheat. God will hear, and he who is before the ages will humble them. God hears me
and humbles them, he who is before the world. They are led by someone, I do not know who, who has come recently [?],
but he who reigned before the world humbles them. For there is no change for them, and they did not fear God. That is because
there is no change in their life, and they did not fear God. He stretched out his hand in repaying. He stretches out his hand to give reward.
At the judgment he repays them. They defiled his testament. They corrupted his testament. How does the scripture say?
IN YOUR SEED SHALL ALL NATIONS BE BLESSED. Whoever is a heretic and schismatic is separated from the body of Christ;
he does not seek the blessing in the seed of Abraham; therefore he does not listen to the testator. They were divided by the wrath of his face, and his heart drew near.
By his wrath they were divided, and then his heart drew near. When the Arians came, then in the Trinity God's [?]
so that your praise may resound over all. They prepared a snare for my feet. They set a snare for my feet.
I walked on earth with rebuke and with promise, as if with two feet. There they lay in wait for me.
And they bowed down my soul. And they made me stoop, for among them I was bowed, not upright.
and their works always looked to the earth. They dug a pit before my face, and they fell into it. They dug pits for me.
and they plunged into them. They were overthrown in them, not I. Whoever wishes to betray another
is himself betrayed. My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready. Now my heart is ready, since you will it so, God.
It is ready to endure their wickedness. I will sing and recite a psalm. Therefore I sing to you, and sing psalms to you thus.
Arise, my glory. Stand up, my glory. Show yourself by rising again and ascending. Arise, psaltery and harp.
Stand up and show yourselves, miracles and sufferings. In the psaltery the strings sound from the upper part.
From there came Christ's miracles. But in the harp they sound from the lower part; from there were Christ's sufferings. Let the psaltery sound,
so the dead rise, and the blind, the lame, the paralysed and the sick are healed. Let the harp sound, that Christ suffers hunger and thirst,
that he sleeps, is seized, is scourged, is mocked, mocked, is crucified, is buried. I will arise at dawn. I arise early.
At daybreak the psaltery and harp arose, that is, the Lord's body. I will confess to you among the peoples, Lord, and I will sing a psalm to you among the nations.
I confess to you among the peoples, Lord, and sing a psalm to you among the nations. That is now fulfilled, for psalms and
the praises of God are in all kingdoms. For your truth is magnified up to the heavens, and your mercy up to the clouds.
For your truth is magnified up to heaven, and your mercy up to the clouds.
This is to be read in reversed order, for truth is pure in the angels, and through mercy it is also shared with the men
who are preachers of the truth. Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and your glory above all the earth. That stands earlier.
UNTO THE END, DESTROY NOT DAVID, FOR AN INSCRIPTION OF A TITLE. That also stands before the previous psalm. IF YOU TRULY SPEAK JUSTICE,
judge what is right, sons of men. Christ says to the Jews: If you children of men speak what is right, then judge it rightly.
Judge it just as you speak it. Many speak what they do not judge that way. They say, if someone asks them,
that good faith is better than treasure, and yet they do not judge it so, for treasure is dearer to them.
If they were in earnest about it, they would show it; then they would not exchange good faith for treasure.
For in your heart you work iniquities on the earth. You work unrighteousness on earth in your heart. All who are on earth
have their hearts full of unrighteousness before it comes to deeds. How does that show?
And therefore they did not see God, who is the true sun. Before your thorns bring forth the bramble,
as if living, as if in wrath, he swallows them up. He says "your thorns" in place of "their thorns." God swallows them up
before their thorns bring forth the bramble. He destroys them before their wickedness grows strong. The thorns on the bramble are soft at first;
after that they become terribly hard and strong. As if they were living, he swallows them up; but they are dead,
though they seem to themselves to be alive. And as if in wrath, when in fact he is acting for good. When he says "he swallows them up,"
it is as if he said: he takes them away and does not let them live as long as they had intended.
The just man shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance. The righteous man rejoices when he sees in the sinners the punishment of the first sin.
That is evil desire, which comes from the first sin. The just man flees from it; therefore he has a pure conscience
and rejoices. He shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner. He washes his hands in the sinner's blood. That is to say,
he becomes better because of the sinner's ruin. As the wise Solomon says: "When the fool perishes, the wise man becomes more astute."
And man shall say: If indeed there is fruit for the just man, then indeed there is a God who judges them on earth. And so people say: If the righteous man gains profit,
if he has his reward even here, then God is on earth, judging over them, before the Day of Judgment comes. So this is true:
he gives the righteous spiritual joy here as an advance payment, and eternal life hereafter.
Unto the end. Destroy not. For David, for an inscription of a title, when Saul sent and watched his house in order to kill him.
David sang this psalm when Saul sent men and besieged his house in order to kill him there.
The other part of this title was explained earlier. Saul signifies the Jews, who set a guard on the sepulchre of Christ
so that they might destroy him in his members. For if they could deny the resurrection, his name would be destroyed.
Against them Christ now prays: Deliver me from my enemies, my God. Free me from my enemies, my God.
And from those who rise up against me set me free. And save me from those who attack me. Deliver me from those who work iniquity.
Free me from those who act unjustly. And from men of blood save me. And protect me from murderers.
For behold, they have seized my soul. For they have captured me. They have brought me into the distress of the Passion.
The strong have rushed upon me. Strong ones have set upon me: the devil and his servants. Neither my iniquity nor my sin,
O Lord. There is no injustice and no sin in me. Without iniquity I ran, and I was directed.
Without injustice I ran, and I turned rightly to where I was meant to go. Even though they are strong,
they cannot follow me. Arise to meet me. Stand up toward me; help me so that I may rise again. And see.
And let them see the direction of my course; that is, so that others may see it and follow me,
and recognize me as like you. And you, O Lord God of hosts, God of Israel. And you, Lord, mighty God, God of Israel,
of a single people, as people suppose. Attend to visit all the nations. Hasten to visit all peoples. Bring them all to faith.
Have no mercy on all who work iniquity. Nor do you forgive it to all who work injustice.
Do not let it go unpunished. Either they themselves pay for it, or you make them pay for it. There are also sins
which God does not forgive. These are the sins of those who say: "If God had not willed it, I would not have done it."
They lay their guilt on God, which is intolerable. They shall return at evening,
and they shall suffer hunger like dogs. At evening they will be converted, that is, at the end of the world. For when Elijah and Enoch come,
then the Jews will become believers. Then they will hunger for the faith, like the Gentiles, whom they called dogs
because the Gentiles seemed unclean to them. And they shall go round about the city. And they go around the city.
They travel around the whole world preaching. What Paul and the other apostles did, they will then do. Behold, they shall speak with their mouth,
and a sword is in their lips. Then they will speak with their mouth what is not now in their mind, and there is a sword in their lips,
that is, the word of God. For who has heard? For who heard it? They say this angrily, which is the sword in their lips:
why do others not hear what they themselves would not hear before? As if they themselves had not been converted
at evening. And you, O Lord, shall laugh at them. And you, Lord, mock those who will not hear your word.
You shall bring all the nations to nothing. You count all unbelieving peoples as nothing. Or it means: for you it is easy,
and as nothing, to convert all peoples. I will keep my strength for you. I keep my strength with you,
because apart from you I do not have it; if I go away from you, I lose it.
For you, God, are my protector. For you are the one who takes me up. I was wicked; I lay in sins; from there you took me
and drew me to you. My God, his mercy shall go before me. He is my God, whose grace goes before me.
I did no good unless he first urged me to it. My God, show me among my enemies.
My God, show me your grace among my enemies, so that they too may be made better
and turn from enemies into friends. Do not slay them, lest at any time they forget your law. Do not slay them,
lest they then forget your law. Do not slay the Jews in that way,
so that they forget your law. Let them endure until evening, and then convert them.
"And Syria Sobal. And he turned Moab, and struck Edom in the Valley of the Salt Pits, twelve thousand." This psalm looks to Christ. It is sung for those
who are to be changed, in keeping with the inscription, so that they turn from King Devil to Christ,
the king of the Jews: to serve David himself, Christ himself, and to give thought to his teaching. So it came about
when the true David burned Mesopotamia of Syria and Syria Sobal. He burned them rightly, as the interpretations of the names show.
Mesopotamia means "exalted calling," Syria "lofty," Sobal "vain oldness." Pride, vanity and oldness were burned by him
who came to send fire on the earth. And he converted Moab, that is, the enemy, and struck Edom, that is, the earthly.
He converted hostile people and earthly people. He struck twelve thousand in the Valley of the Salt Pits.
Those settled toward the twelve winds he made to live in humility and in the savor of wisdom, dead to the world, living to God.
"O God, you have cast us off and destroyed us." In these words Christians thank Christ for changing them.
You, God, have thrust us back, because you did not allow us to go the wrong way.
And you tore us down so that we might be built up better. "You were angry." You were angry at the old error.
"And you have had mercy on us." And you took pity on us, teaching us newness of life. "You have moved the earth."
You shook the earth: you made sinners recognize themselves. "And you have troubled it." And you brought it into fear
and also into sorrow. "Heal its breaches, for it is moved." Heal the crushing of their minds, for they have been moved to penitence.
Comfort them with pardon. "You have shown your people hard things." You showed your people hard and toilsome things
in persecution. "You have made us drink the wine of compunction." You gave us the wine of compunction to drink. What is that wine?
"You have given a sign to those who fear you." You gave a sign to those who fear you, in the distresses of persecution,
"so that they may flee from before the bow." So that they may flee before the bow that shoots at sinners.
The faster someone wants to shoot, the farther back the string of the bow is drawn.
God also delays judgment so that it may be all the sharper. "So that your beloved may be delivered." So that your beloved ones may be delivered.
So that they may be delivered by fleeing the bow, hard things happen to them here.
"Save me with your right hand." Preserve me with your right hand, since I must suffer worldly distress.
"And hear me." And hear me, for prayer for heavenly goods is worthier to you than prayer for earthly ones.
"God has spoken in his holy one." God the Father spoke in his holy Son Christ, saying that it shall go this way.
"I will rejoice." I, his people, am glad of this. "And I will divide Shechem," that is, "shoulders." And I divide the shoulders.
who bear the burden of the Lord, in the varied distribution of the Holy Spirit. The idols were buried by Jacob in Shechem. Therefore
the place signifies the gentiles, who afterwards offered their shoulders to the burden of Christian devotion.
And I will measure out the valley of tabernacles, that is, the people of the Jews. And the valley of the encampments, where Jacob stalled his sheep,
I measure out for myself as a share. I am gathered from Jews and gentiles. Gilead is mine, that is, the heap of witness. The multitude of martyrs is mine.
From them too I am gathered. And Manasseh is mine, that is, forgotten. Forgetfulness of my persecution will yet come to me
when I may dwell in peace. And Ephraim, that is, fruitfulness, is the strength of my head. And the strength of my head is my fruitfulness.
The death of Christ is my multiplication. THE DEAD GRAIN OF WHEAT BRINGS FORTH MUCH FRUIT. Judah is my king. I acknowledge the inscription.
CHRIST is my king. Moab, that is, the gentiles, is the pot of my hope. The people that came from an unlawful union, that is the pot of my hope.
Because it has become a pot, because it has been fired in the fire of persecution, therefore it has shown me the hope of its salvation, not of its consumption.
Into Idumea, that is, the earthly, I will stretch out my shoe. Even to those who lead an earthly life I stretch out my shoe.
I send thither feet shod in the preparation of the gospel of peace. To me the foreigners are subject. Strangers worship me, says CHRIST.
WHO ARE NOT TO REIGN WITH ME. Who will lead me into the city of the surrounding region? That is, among the gentiles, who are spread around the one nation of the Jews.
Who leads my preachers to all the peoples settled all around the Jews? Who but God? Who will lead me even into Idumea?
Who makes me known even to those who do not wish to profit from me? Is it not you, O God, who have cast us off? Do
you not do it, you who thrust us away from the old error? As the psalm said earlier?
And you will not go forth, that is, you will not appear, in our forces. You do not show yourself in our strength as you did in the time of Moses
and Joshua son of Nun, and David, when hostile gentiles could not resist us. Inwardly you teach us,
inwardly you strengthen us. If we wished to fight, the fight would be for the present life, not for the future one.
Give us help from tribulation. Give us all the more help in tribulation, since people think we are without help from you.
And vain is the salvation of man. Give us help, give us salvation; give it to us inwardly. The outward salvation of man
is vain. In God we shall do valiantly, and not by the sword. In God we show the virtue of patience, not of resistance.
And he will bring to nothing those who afflict us. And he brings to nothing those who afflict us. As is now evident: where are they?
UNTO THE END, IN HYMNS, TO DAVID HIMSELF. This psalm looks to Christ, sung in praise of David himself, of CHRIST himself.
HEAR, O GOD, MY SUPPLICATION; attend to my prayer. Hear, O God, my plea; look to my prayer,
take heed of it. Who says this? THE FAITHFUL PEOPLE. From the ends of the earth I have cried to you. I cried out to you.
according to the prophecy of Jeremiah and Ezekiel. When did he sing it? When he saw in the prophetic spirit that they would begin to depart from there.
There we see how Paul said: "NOW THESE THINGS HAPPENED TO THEM IN FIGURE." In our times, those are in captivity
who are in desire [of the world]. But those who begin to go from there to love, David means them; to them he sings this song of joy.
A HYMN BEFITS YOU, O GOD, IN ZION. That is the voice of those going out of captivity. To you, God, a song of praise is fitting in Zion, not in Babylon.
Those who have their hope in Zion sing in Zion; they sing in contemplation. And to you shall the vow be paid in Jerusalem.
And the vow shall be fulfilled to you in Jerusalem. He who here has united himself to God as a living sacrifice
will become it more fully in the heavenly Jerusalem. There he will become a holocaust, that is, wholly burnt.
Everything mortal, everything corruptible will there be consumed in him by the divine fire. Hear my prayer; to you all flesh shall come.
that is, from every kind of flesh. Hear my prayer; to you come people of every kind. From every nation, from every condition come those
who become a holocaust there. The words of the wicked have prevailed over us. The teaching of wicked forefathers overpowered us.
They led us to Jupiter and to Mercury. Through their fault we worshipped wood and stones, the works of our hands.
And you will be merciful to our impieties. And you, the priest, will atone for our evils, when you offer yourself to the Father as the evening sacrifice;
then the error will be forgiven. Blessed is he whom you have chosen and taken up. Blessed is the man whom you chose
and took to yourself. He shall dwell in your courts. He dwells in your courts. It is one man,
one faithful people, whose head is Christ. He chose him, he gave him a dwelling. He bids him be where he himself is.
We shall be filled with the good things of your house. We shall be filled with the good that is in your house. Which good?
WHAT EYE HAS NOT SEEN, NOR EAR HEARD, NOR HAS IT ENTERED INTO THE HEART OF MAN. Or as it says next:
Your temple is holy, wonderful in justice. That your holy house is wonderful in righteousness: with that fullness you fill us.
He will be filled with blessedness who makes himself a holy temple for you, wonderful in justice. Hear us, O God our savior.
Our savior, hear us. The hope of all the ends of the earth and of those far off on the sea. The hope of all the ends of the earth,
the hope of the outermost just as of the innermost; the hope of those who live far away in the sea,
among those turned to the world, who are far from you because they are bad fish, breaking the nets. Preparing the mountains in your strength.
Preparing preachers against them in your strength, not in their own. Girded about with power. Surrounded by your majesty.
Or surrounded by those to whom you gave the power of miracles, to all of whom you are common and in whose midst you stand. You who trouble the depths of the sea.
Through their preaching you trouble the bottom of the sea, that is, you stir up the hearts of unbelievers to persecution. Who shall bear the sound of its waves?
He set them firm in life. "For you have tested us, O God; you have tried us by fire as silver is tried by fire." As is plain from this:
For you tested us. You put us in the fire, as one does with silver. There we were purified, not melted away.
"You led us into the snare." You brought us into the snare, where our bodies were caught and our souls were set free.
"You laid troubles on our back; you set men over our heads." You loaded hardships onto our back. Where did they come from?
From this, that you set men over our heads. You let sinners rule over us. "We passed through fire and water."
We have passed through fire and water. We were so tempered in the fire that we could not
perish in the water. Adversity strengthened us; prosperity did not make us soft. "And you brought us out into refreshment."
And by doing this you brought us into the coolness of eternal rest, where it is neither
too hot nor too cold, and where there is no temptation of either kind, of fire or of water. "I will go into your house with burnt offerings."
With burnt offerings I go into your house, where the divine fire burns up the corruption of the flesh and the impurity of the soul.
There I become an offering, as a whole burnt offering. "I will pay you my vows." There I will fulfil my promises to you,
the promises of eternal praise. "Which my lips distinguished." Which my lips always distinguished,
because I always made promises of your praise, not of my own, for I recognized that I am changeable and you are unchangeable, that without you I am nothing,
but that you do not need me. "And my mouth spoke in my tribulation." And in my distress in the world my mouth spoke. What did it say?
"I will offer you burnt offerings full of marrow." I bring you offerings rich in marrow. I love you in my bones. But a person does not do this
who wants to please people more than God. "With the incense of rams." With smoke, that is, prayers. Whose prayers?
Those of the wise men and leaders of God's flocks, that is, the apostles, who pray most of all for the flocks.
"I will offer you oxen with goats." I bring you cattle together with the goats: preachers together with sinners.
The goats would not be acceptable if the fruits of the trees did not help them. To them it is said:
"Make friends for yourselves of the mammon of iniquity, so that when you fail they may receive you into eternal dwellings."
Holy Church has brought such offerings to God, and this is her voice in her tribulation.
"Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell how much he has done for my soul." Come here, all you who fear God,
listen, and I will tell you what God has done for my soul. "I cried to him with my mouth." That means this:
With my mouth I called out to him. From then on he was mine, from the time he began to be the true one to me.
The one was false and foreign whom my pagan parents taught me [?] to wood and stones. "And I exalted under my tongue."
And I exalted him secretly under my tongue, in the privacy of my heart.
That he granted to my soul; that I will boast of to you all. If I have regarded iniquity in my heart, God will not hear.
If I had regarded wrong in my heart and loved it, then God would not hear my prayer. Therefore
God has heard, and has attended to the voice of my supplication. Because I did not do so, therefore God heard me,
and therefore he listened to the voice of my prayer. Blessed be God, who has not taken away my prayer
nor his mercy from me. Praised be the God who did not take my supplication away from me,
nor his grace. When he did not let me grow weary of supplication, then he willed to show me grace.
A PSALM OF DAVID. MAY GOD HAVE MERCY ON US AND BLESS US. May God be gracious to us, and bless us.
The rain of his teaching, the rain of his instruction, may he give us; the blessing of eternal life may he give us.
May he make his face shine upon us. The face of the sun he makes shine upon the good and the wicked.
May he make his own face shine over us, so that we may see it.
Or else it is understood thus: may his image, which he gave us, be lit up in us with the light of wisdom.
And may he have mercy on us. And in that shining may he be gracious to us. To what does that lead us?
That we may know your way upon earth. That we, Lord, here in this earth may know Christ, your way,
who leads to you. Your salvation among all nations. And that we may know your Savior, that same Christ, among all peoples.
Let the peoples confess to you, O God; let all the peoples confess to you. What will happen then? Then the peoples will confess to you, God;
all peoples will confess to you. Let them confess their own iniquity and the grace of God; let them accuse themselves and praise him. Let the nations rejoice and exult.
In that confession let the peoples rejoice and leap for joy. What gladdens them? Because you judge the peoples in equity.
For you judge over the peoples according to right and according to their conscience. And you will direct the nations on earth. And the crookedly walking peo-
-ples you direct on earth to the right way. Let the peoples confess to you, O God; let all the peoples confess to you. The earth has yielded its fruit.
The earth brought forth its fruit. Where did it come from? Only from their confession. After penitence and after confession came good works.
May God, our God, bless us; may God bless us. May the Holy Trinity bless us. Blessing aims at multiplication; therefore it says next:
And let all the ends of the earth fear him. And may all the ends of the earth fear him. Let the multiplication come about from that.
UNTO THE END, FOR DAVID HIMSELF, A PSALM OF A SONG. In a psalm there is resonance; in a song, joy.
Here are both; therefore this song is a psalm of a song. LET GOD ARISE AND LET HIS ENEMIES BE SCATTERED.
Why are they called kings (reges)? Because they rule (regentes) the desires of the flesh. How does he distinguish them
among themselves? As it says: AND HE GAVE SOME AS APOSTLES, SOME AS PROPHETS, AND SOME AS EVANGELISTS,
AND SOME AS TEACHERS AND PASTORS. How? With snow in the shade, because the grace of the Holy Spirit gives them shade
against the heats of the flesh. Selmon is the name of a certain mountain in Palestine. I do not mean that one. The mountain of God, I call a fertile mountain.
I mean the visible Christ, the highest mountain of God: abundant, fruitful, full of milk
for nourishing little ones with milk. Why do you suspect other fertile mountains? This is the mountain in which it has pleased God to dwell.
Why do you suppose other mountains to be fruitful? Why do you think any one of them is a mountain so pleasing to God as a dwelling place?
For he himself said: THE FATHER WHO DWELLS IN ME, HE DOES THE WORKS. I AM IN THE FATHER AND THE FATHER IS IN ME. For the Lord will dwell
that is, in those fertile mountains, until the end. As God dwells in him, so he dwells in them, according to the words: I IN THEM
AND YOU IN ME. How long? Until he brings them to the end, which is he himself. The chariot of God: they are God's chariots.
Therefore he sits in them, therefore he guides them, until he brings them to the end. Ten thousand times manifold. Ten-thousandfold,
that is, manifold, because there is no counting them. Thousands of those who rejoice. A thousand joyful ones. Why should they not be?
The Lord is among them. The Lord is within them; therefore they rejoice. In Sinai, in the holy place. That is, in the commandment, which is holy.
God is within them and establishes them in his holy commandment. You have ascended on high, you have led captivity captive, you have received gifts among men.
You, CHRIST, ascended to heaven; you made captive the captivity of men; you slew death.
You received various gifts in them. Because they are your body, their gifts are therefore yours. And from these gifts some became
apostles, some prophets, some teachers. Such you made them. What were they before? Not believing that the Lord God dwells among them.
Unbelieving. In what? That God should dwell in them. They did not trust that God would dwell in them
and that they would become chariots of God; you made them believe this. BLESSED BE THE LORD FROM DAY TO DAY. For this let God be praised
from day to day, because he still is, and always will be, leading captivity captive and receiving gifts among men.
The God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous, our God, the God of saving. God of our salvation, our God, God of saving:
he makes our journey go forward. He makes the course of life prosperous. And the Lord's are the ways out of death. And the departure of the Lord's death:
what does it do? It makes our journey prosperous. Or it means: the departure of death also belongs to the Saviour. Since he died innocent,
why then should we not take comfort in it, guilty and sinners as we are? But God will shatter the heads of his enemies,
the hairy crown of those who walk on in their offences. But although he suffered death, he shattered the heads of his enemies.
and the crowns of the hair of those who go on in their misdeeds. As it says: "Raise me up, and I will repay them."
The Lord said: from Bashan, that is, from dryness, I will turn them back; I will turn them back from the depths of the sea. Thus the Lord promised.
From dryness I turn them to greenness. From the depths of the sea, that is, from the perils of the world, I turn them back.
I take them out of the waves of vices. "That your foot may be dipped in blood." So inwardly do you turn them to yourself,
that your foot may be dipped in the blood of martyrdom together with them. They are your members; in them you suffer persecution. "The tongue of your dogs
[?] from the enemies, from him." Those who were formerly your enemies become the tongue of your dogs. They become your preachers.
From where does this come to them? From where, if not from him, the very one who turned them back from Bashan and from the depths of the sea?
"Your goings in were seen, O God." Your goings in, God, were seen here in the world, and also in your own incarnation,
and also when you came on the clouds, of which you said: "Henceforth you shall see the Son of Man coming on the clouds."
They are also your chariot, on which you have ridden through all this world. "The goings of my God, my King,
that is, were seen, who is in the holy place." The goings of my God, of my King, who is in his holy temple. Which are these?
Those who are also clouds and a chariot. "The princes went before, joined to those singing psalms, in the midst of young maidens playing timbrels."
The apostles came first; right after them others who followed them were joined to them, singing God's praise in voice and in deed.
They came and were set in charge in the midst of the new churches, which sing with timbrels, because they lived in the mortification of the flesh,
just as a timbrel is made from dried and stretched leather. "In the churches bless God." The churches are the timbrel-playing maidens.
In them they praise God. "The Lord from the fountains of Israel." Praise the Lord from the springs of Israel. The first fountains,
I mean the apostles, who came from Israel. They were fountains; they were the springs.
From them came rivers. "There is Benjamin, the younger." There among the fountains was Paul, of the tribe of Benjamin,
"the younger," that is, the last of the apostles. "In ecstasy," that is, in a going out of the mind. In being startled,
as he was startled when he heard from heaven: "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" Or it means: in that
departure of the mind, as happened when he was caught up to the third heaven. "The princes of Judah," that is, of confession,
"their leaders. The princes of Zebulun," that is, of strength; "the princes of Naphtali," that is, of breadth. The apostles were princes of confession, of strength, of breadth,
that is, of faith, hope, and charity. "Command, O God, your strength." Commend to us, O God, your strength. Make Christ dear to us, God the Father,
who is your strength. Teach us to love him who died for us. "Confirm, O God, what you have wrought in us."
Make firm, God, the faith that you gave us. "From your temple, which is in Jerusalem, kings shall offer you gifts."
Away from your house, which is in the lower Jerusalem, kings bring you gifts in the upper Jerusalem.
These are the ones who here subdue the desires of the flesh. "Rebuke the wild beasts of the reed." Rebuke the beasts of the reed.
Rebuke the heretics, the enemies of Holy Scripture. "The herd of bulls among the cows of the peoples, so that they may be shut out", that is, so that they may stand out,
those who have been tested like silver. These same heretics then go about like so many bulls among the people's cows. Who are these?
None other than stubborn and misled people, like the cows that follow the bulls; so that those may be raised up
who are praiseworthy in the divine scriptures. As Paul said: "There must also be heresies, so that those who are approved may be made manifest among you."
The wickedness of the heretics makes the goodness and the wisdom of the catholics shine. Therefore it says here:
"Excludantur" means "exprimantur" (let them be pressed out, made to stand out). Just as the makers of silver vessels are also called "exclusores". "Scatter the nations that want wars."
Scatter, Lord, the heretics, who are called "nations" not because of the generations of families but because of
the kinds of sects. Destroy them before they gain a succession. "Let them bring quickly out of Egypt."
Let the nations quickly bring their souls to God out of Egypt, out of the darkness; let all nations hasten to him.
"Let Ethiopia hasten to give its hands to God." Let Ethiopia hasten to hold out its hands to God, hasten to surrender to him, as the defeated do in war.
According to Jerome it reads thus. "Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing psalms to the Lord." For such manifold grace
sing to God, all kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord. "Sing psalms to God, who ascended above the heaven of heavens toward the east."
Sing praises to God, who went up above all the heavens before his disciples at Jerusalem, which is in the eastern regions; or else "toward the east"
means toward the Father. "Behold, he will give his voice, a voice of power." When he comes from there to judge, then he will make his voice known,
the voice of power, that is, "Come" or "Go". Then he who once wished to be silent will become very loud.
"Give glory to God; his magnificence is over Israel." Glorify God, for then his greatness will come over Israel;
then he will magnify the faithful people. "And his power is in the clouds." And then his power will shine in the clouds,
in the apostles and prophets, who here were clouds and there become judges. "God is wonderful in his saints, the God of Israel."
Then the God of Israel will become wonderful in his saints, the God of the one who sees God. "He himself will give power and strength to his people;
blessed be God." Then he will give his people the power of the resurrection, the strength of incorruption. May God be praised for this.
UNTO THE END, FOR THOSE WHO SHALL BE CHANGED, TO DAVID HIMSELF. This psalm is sung to David himself, to Christ himself.
In it he himself tells us of his passion, by which we were redeemed and changed from mortal life
to eternal life; changed from earthly life to heavenly life, from corruptible life to incorruption. SAVE ME, O GOD.
Let those who wait for you, Lord, not be put to shame because of me, Lord of hosts. Let those who wait for you, Lord, not be put to shame because of me,
Lord of powers. Let no one say to them: "Where is he who said to you, BELIEVE IN GOD AND BELIEVE ALSO IN ME?" Let them not be con-
-founded because of me, those who seek you, God of Israel. And do not allow my enemies so much power against me
that those who seek you, God of Israel, are ashamed of me. For it is for your sake that I have endured reproach.
Shamelessness has covered my face. For I suffered reproach because of you, and because of you shamelessness covered my face.
If anyone said to me, "You are a Christian, a worshipper of the crucified one," I felt no shame at that and did not hold back from it.
I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to the sons of my mother. I have become a stranger and a foreigner to my mother's children.
I am a son of the synagogue, and still they say: "BUT AS FOR THIS MAN, WE DO NOT KNOW WHERE HE COMES FROM." Why is that?
For zeal for your house has consumed me. For zeal for your house devoured me. That is the reason: I zealously punished their wrongdoing.
That is why they did not see fit to acknowledge me. If they acknowledged what is right, they would acknowledge me, and then I would be without zeal against them.
And the insults of those who insulted you have fallen on me. And the insults of those who insulted you came upon me. Why is that?
Because no one reviles me without also reviling you: I and you are one. And I covered my soul with fasting,
and that became a reproach to me. I covered my soul with fasting, and that too became a reproach to me.
When I hungered for them and they were bitter to me, I would not take them into my body as they were.
I chose to fast from them. I would not consent to their wickedness, and for that they reproached me. And I made sackcloth my garment,
that is, I set my flesh before them so that they could vent their rage on it, but I hid my divinity from them. I offered them my garment of haircloth,
my mortal body, so that they could commit their crime against it and destroy themselves, and their crime might become atonement for others.
And I became a byword to them, that is, an object of mockery. I became a comparison to them, a mocking comparison: "Just as it happened to that one,"
they said, "so may it happen to him. Just as that one perished, so may this one perish. That one was evil,
and evil came upon him. This one is evil; may nothing better come upon him either." Those who sat in the gate insulted me,
that is, in public. Those who sat at the city gate, where people went in and out, mocked me.
There they held me up to scorn. And those who drank wine made songs about me. They sat drinking wine
and sang about me. Many still do the same: they sing about anyone who keeps them from their wrongdoing. But I [directed] my prayer
that is, I directed it to you, Lord. But I prayed to you for them: FATHER, FORGIVE THEM, FOR THEY DO NOT KNOW WHAT THEY ARE DOING.
A time of good pleasure, O God; that is, the time of your good pleasure has come. A favourable time is still coming, God the Father. When?
In the multitude of your mercy. In the manifoldness of your grace, by which your Son rises from death,
and mankind together with him. Hear me in the truth of your salvation. Hear me in the truth of your salvation.
The salvation that you promised, which you will grant: in that, hear me. Save me from the mud, so that I do not stick fast. Of which he said above:
I AM STUCK FAST IN THE MIRE OF THE DEEP. Free me out of the mire, so that I do not stick fast in it. Of whom do you speak?
Deliver me from those who hate me. I say: free me from those who hate me. They are the mire. And from the depth of the waters.
And from the depth of the waters. These are all the same people. They roar in their storm like rushing waters.
Let not the tempest of water drown me. So says the body of Christ. Let not the storm of the waters drown me. In the flesh it has done
it, as stands above: AND THE TEMPEST HAS DROWNED ME. In the spirit let them not do it. Let me not become one who consents to them; then I will not go into the depth of the mire.
Then they will not swallow me; then I will not go into their body, for I am the body of Christ.
Let everyone take care that his body does not come into their power. But if it should happen, let him pray for the soul,
that they may not gain power over it. Nor let the deep swallow me up. Nor let the deep swallow me up.
Nor let the pit close its mouth over me. Nor let the pit shut its opening over me. Whoever plunges into sin
