in parables and mysteries, until they were full, together with the fat of the wheat. And they say this, giving the solution to many deep matters [?].
NOTHING BETTER, NOTHING SWEETER CAN BE UNDERSTOOD OR SPOKEN. AND YET THE ENEMIES OF THE LORD LIED TO HIM.
A PSALM FOR ASAPH HIMSELF. This psalm is sung for Asaph himself, that is, for the synagogue itself, and to it he promises the coming of the Lord.
GOD STOOD IN THE SYNAGOGUE OF THE GODS. Christ came here and stood here, visible, in the midst of the assembly of the gods,
that is, of the Israelites, of whom he says further on: I SAID, YOU ARE GODS, AND ALL OF YOU SONS OF THE MOST HIGH.
And in the midst he judges between the gods. Standing there in the midst, he separates them, making out of the same lump some vessels for honor
and others for dishonor. How long will you judge unjustly and accept the persons of sinners? How long, you Israelites, will you keep doing this,
judging wrong to be right and showing favor to the persons of sinners? Those who were disobedient to the law
killed the prophets and now want to kill Christ. How long will you follow them and be like them in appearance?
You are the people of God, and you are such a great multitude that the princes must fear you. How can you be guiltless
if you let them do such evil? For your sake Christ has become needy and an orphan. Judge for the needy and the orphan.
Therefore secure justice for him, as is right: stand up to protect him. No one dares to kill him unless you are willing. Justify the humble and the poor. The princes,
proud and grown rich in themselves, do not think him righteous. But you should regard Christ, who has become lower for your sake, as the only righteous one.
Rescue the poor man. Take the poor man away from there. And free the needy from the hand of the sinner. And set the wretched man free
from the hands of the sinner, so that you too do not become sinful by consenting, and do not follow them in this:
that you demand Barabbas for life and Christ for death. They did not know and did not understand; they walk in darkness.
They did not know these things and did not perceive them. For if they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of majesty.
They walk in darkness because they are blinded, and not they alone, but you along with them. All the foundations of the earth will be shaken.
Therefore all the foundations of the earth will be shaken. For there were earthquakes then, when these blind men crucified Christ.
Or it means that those founded on earthly happiness were moved to wonder at the signs and to repentance for their sins
when these men were blinded. As Paul said: BLINDNESS HAS COME UPON PART OF ISRAEL, UNTIL THE FULLNESS OF THE GENTILES SHOULD COME IN.
I said, You are gods, and all of you sons of the Most High. But you shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes. How so, you Jews?
I said, You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High. That is what I wanted you to be, beings who do not die. But you die,
as men who were once gods must do, and you are not exalted as sons of the Most High. Instead you fall through pride of heart.
Like one of the princes, that is, the devil. That is rebuke and reproach. Arise, O God, judge the earth. Stand up, God, from death, and judge
over the earthly ones who sat in judgment over you; judge them, the earth-dwellers, on the last day.
For you shall inherit among all nations. For you possess all nations through faith and love.
A canticle of a psalm of Asaph. The loudest song is Asaph's. This speaks to the congregation of the people of God about the second coming of the Lord. O GOD, WHO SHALL BE LIKE YOU?
When you come, Christ, to judge, who will then be like you? In your first coming you were like human beings, and you were even like robbers,
for you appeared in the form of a servant. But when you come in glory, who can then be found like you? Do not keep silent, and do not hold back, O God.
Since you kept silent when you came hidden, now that you come openly, do not keep silent and do not hold back your judgment.
For behold, your enemies have made an uproar, and those who hate you have lifted up their head. For your enemies were very loud,
and they raised up their head, the Antichrist, whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of his mouth. Against your people they have devised a malicious plan,
and they have plotted against your saints. They devised an evil plan against your people and plotted against your saints.
They said: thus they spoke: Come, and let us destroy them from among the nations. Come, let us gather together; let us wipe them out from among the peoples,
so that they may no longer exist among the peoples. And let the name of Israel be remembered no more. And let the name of Israel no longer be mentioned.
For they have plotted together with one mind. For they plotted together in agreement. Against you they have made a covenant. They made a pact against you.
Testamentum means both things: the kind that has no force until the testators are dead, and also every pact and agreement is called a
testamentum, as when Jacob and Laban made a testamentum that they were to keep while they were still alive. The tents of the Edomites and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagarenes,
Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, the foreigners together with the inhabitants of Tyre. These made the pact. Their names show that they are God's enemies.
Edomites: earthly, or bloody. Ishmaelites: obedient to themselves, that is, not to God but to themselves. Moab: from the father,
because his mother conceived him by her own father in an unlawful way. Hagarenes: proselytes, that is, newcomers, who have the mind of strangers, not of fellow citizens,
who show their true selves once they find a chance to do harm. Gebal: empty valley, that is, falsely humble. Ammon: a troubled people, or a people of sorrow.
Amalek: a licking people, as it is said: HIS ENEMIES SHALL LICK THE DUST. Foreigners: born elsewhere, and for that reason enemies. Tyre:
distress, or tribulation. For Assyria too came with them. The devil himself came along with them. They came to help the children of Lot,

that is, of the one who turns aside. The devil is the one who turns aside from God, and his angels are the children of the one who turns aside. These people came to help them. Whatever they want to do,
they and their father the devil, the children of unbelief help them with it. Do to them as you did to Midian and Sisera, and to Jabin at the brook Kishon.
Deal with them as you dealt with Midian, whose name in Latin means 'turning aside judgment', and with Sisera, whose name means 'exclusion of joy'.
and Jabin, whose name means "wise" — not for good but for evil. They were defeated at the brook Kishon,
which in Latin means "their hardness." They perished at Endor. They were lost in the "fountain of generation," because they did not seek the fountain of regeneration,
in which they could have been saved. They became like the dung of the earth. They became like the dung of the earth, they who could not
bring forth anything but earthly birth. Make their princes like Oreb and Zeb and Zebah and Zalmunna. Set their princes — how?
As you once set Oreb, whose name means "dryness," and Zeb, whose name means "wolf," and Zebah, whose name means "victim" —
whose victim? The wolf's, of course — and Zalmunna, whose name means "shadow of commotion." All their princes, who said: Let us take possession of the sanctuary of God as an inheritance.
In this way all their princes will be destroyed, who said to one another: Let us take possession of God's temple.
What is the temple but the people of God? They are always eager to turn that people to their own will. That is "empty sound,"
which is why it says earlier: YOUR ENEMIES HAVE MADE A NOISE. My God, make them like a wheel. My God, make them unsteady in their counsel,
like a wheel. Or else: a wheel rises at the back and falls at the front. In the same way the Lord's enemies rise here among the lowest goods;
further on, among the best, they fall; there they fail. And like stubble before the face of the wind.
And like the stalk before the wind. Give them light hearts, so that they cannot stand firm before temptation. Like the fire that burns up the forest
and like the flame that burns up the mountains, so you will pursue them with your storm, and in your anger you will trouble them. But when? At the judgment.
On the last day you will pursue them with your storm, and in your anger you will trouble them, coming as terribly
as the fire that burns the forest and the flame that burns the mountains. In this verse, "you will pursue" and "you will trouble" mean the same thing,
and so do "with storm" and "in anger," and "fire" and "flame." But understand "forest" as the barren, and "mountains" as the proud.
Fill their faces with shame, and they will seek your name, O Lord. Fill their faces with disgrace, and then they will seek
your name, Lord. Fight them with adversities, and then they will begin to flee to you. Those who do not do this —
what will happen to them? Let them be ashamed and troubled for ever and ever, and let them be confounded and perish.
Let them be ashamed and troubled and disgraced and lost, for ever and ever. And let them know that your name is Lord.
And so let both those and these know that you are called Lord, and that others are lords only as servants,
and so are still lords subject to your command. Let them learn that. And what else? That you alone are the Most High over all the earth.
That you alone are called the Most High over all the earth. Why then do those who are on the earth, and are themselves earth, raise themselves against you?
UNTO THE END, FOR THE WINEPRESSES, A PSALM FOR THE SONS OF KORAH. This psalm looks to Christ. It is sung about the winepresses, for the sons of the bald one.
The churches of God are winepresses. They are press-houses. In them are the Christians, who are trodden down in the pressures of many persecutions.
The earlier generation, the one that was before Christ, was lost. The one that comes after is saved through baptism.
O God, you will turn and bring us to life. Lord, by turning us with your calling, you bring us to life.
When we flee from you, you turn us back to you and save us. And your people shall rejoice in you. And your people rejoices in you,
not in itself. Show us your mercy, O Lord, and grant us your salvation. Show us your grace, Lord,
and give us Christ, your Savior: to be seen not only in the flesh, but in his divinity,
according to the promise: "for we shall see him as he is." I will hear what the Lord God speaks in me.
I listen for myself to what the Lord God speaks in me. Let the noise of the world not disturb me, but let me be able to perceive
what the Holy Spirit says to me. For he will speak peace to his people, and to his saints, and to those who turn to him.
For he promises peace to his people, and to his saints, and to those who turn to him. When does
that come? When this bodily nature puts on incorruption and this mortal nature puts on immortality. Do not let it seem long to you, Christian. Here you have war;
here you must fight; there you shall rest. Yet his salvation is near to those who fear him, that glory may dwell in our land.
Yet his Savior does appear in the flesh among those who fear him: he will be born among the Jews,
so that glory may dwell in our land together with us, who were always his. Mercy and truth have met each other.
Truth and grace met each other. Gentiles and Jews came to one faith. For the Gentiles it is mercy;
for the Jews it is truth. Or: the truth of the Old Testament agrees with the mercy of the New Testament. Justice and peace have kissed.
Justice and peace kissed each other. They were always friends. Where there is justice, there is peace. That leads to peace:
that you do not do to another what you do not want for yourself. If you keep [?] to that, then you have made [?] peace. Truth has sprung from the earth,
and justice has looked down from heaven. Christ was born of Mary, and therefore justice looked upon us from heaven.
Through heavenly grace we were justified when Christ came here. Truth also comes from the earth
when a person makes a true confession, and heavenly justice follows it, for by that he is justified. So it happened to the publican,
who called himself a sinner. For the Lord will give sweetness, and our land will yield its fruit. Truly, God gives the sweetness of justice;
he makes us desire what is better. And our land will yield its fruit. And from that our fields bear their crop.
He visits our hearts; from that we begin to do good. Justice will walk before him, and will set his steps
on the way. Justice goes before. Which justice? Penance and confession.
By that he turns his steps onto the way that leads to our hearts. In this way one must prepare the way of the Lord.
Your truth shall be prepared in the heavens. In the holy preachers your truth will be prepared.
That also makes me sing. I have made a covenant with my chosen. You also said: I have appointed for my chosen ones a testament.
Which is that? None other than the New Testament, by which we are renewed by the Lord for the inheritance that is in heaven.
I have sworn to David my servant. You also said: I swore to my servant David. How was the oath made?
Thus I swore to him: I will prepare your seed forever. To eternity I prepare your seed,
that is, Christ and those who believe in him. And I will build up your throne from generation to generation. And I build your seat in all generations.
Here is the earthly generation; God sits in it, because he governs it. After this comes the heavenly one,
in which he sits again, because he reigns in it. Then they become heavens by carrying God. From this there follows at once:
The heavens shall confess your wonders, O Lord. The heavens tell your wonders, Lord. They do not tell of their own merit;
they praise you. And your truth in the church of the saints. And they tell your truth in the congregation of the
saints. When the heavens give dew, they wet the lands, which bear good fruit. For who among the clouds shall be equal to the Lord?
For they tell the truth to the church of the saints when they say: Who will be made equal to God among the clouds?
They are heavens because of the brightness of the truth; they are clouds because of the hidden things of the flesh. Who can see through clouds? And who knows what lies hidden in the flesh?
Was Christ not also a cloud? Was he not covered with flesh? Which of the clouds was like him? And who among the sons of God shall be like God?
And who among the sons of God is like God? What they are by grace, he is by nature. God, who is glorified in the council of the saints.
He is the God who is glorified in the council of the saints. Their counsel is to believe in him, whom they cannot be like.
In this way they glorify him. Great and terrible over all who are round about him. Great and terrible over all the sons of God who are around him,
because they are near him. Or they are 'around him' because he was born, died, was buried and rose again in Jerusalem,
and the nations are settled all around it. And there he thundered from his own cloud, and then he sent out other clouds to water the nations round about.
As he promised in the Passion: Hereafter you shall see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven. Lord God of hosts, who is like you?
Lord God of powers, who is like you? Though others may have power, they do not have it of themselves.
You are mighty, O Lord, and your truth is round about you. You, Lord, are mighty, and your truth is around you.
In yourself you are mighty; from you comes your truth in the others. You rule
the power of the sea. You are so mighty that you even rule the power of the sea. If the sea rose up against their truth,
that need not move them. Why? But you calm the motion of its waves. Because you still its waves.
You measured out the persecutions of the wicked. You humbled the proud one like one who is wounded. The devil himself you brought low, struck down as if by a wound.
That in which he gloried, you took from him. And with the arm of your strength you scattered your enemies.
And by your strength you scattered your enemies, the Jews and the persecutors. Yours are the heavens, and yours is the earth.
Yours are the heavens, from which the truth rains down; yours is the earth, which is watered from there. Or thus:
Yours are the heavens, in which the devil wished to rule; yours is the earth, on which the Jews wished to rage against you. The circle of the earth and its fullness you founded.
The circle of the earth and all that is in it you have founded; therefore you rule over it, and they can do nothing against you.
You created the north and the sea. The north and the sea you created. However much the devil may be in the north, as he said:
I WILL SET MY THRONE IN THE NORTH, and however much storm there may be on the sea, they can still do nothing against your will.
Tabor, that is, 'coming light,' and Hermon, that is, 'his anathema' (understood: the devil's), will rejoice in your name.
Tabor and Hermon are mountains of Syria. Those are also mountains whose light, that is, faith, coming from Christ, makes them renounce the devil.
They rightly rejoice, God, in your name. Your arm is with power. Your arm is mighty, both for fighting and for defending. Let be strength-
-ened your hand, and let your right hand be exalted. Let your hand grow strong to press down the proud, and let your right hand be exalted to glorify the humble.
Justice and judgment are the preparation of your throne. Righteousness and judgment are the preparation of your seat on the last day.
Therefore you will set some at the right hand and others at the left. But how is it now? Mercy and truth shall go before your face.
Now, in the meantime before that, mercy and truth go before your face. Mercy, because you will blot out sins;
truth, because you promised so. Blessed is the people that knows jubilation. Blessed is the people that knows that joy,
that can recognize how it should rejoice in these two. Lord, they shall walk in the light of your countenance.
Those who know this walk, Lord, in your light. You reveal it to them. And in your name they shall rejoice all the day.
And in your name they rejoice at all times. Those who do not rejoice in this way do not persevere in their joy.
And in your justice they shall be exalted. And in your righteousness they are exalted, not in their own righteousness.
The Jews wished to establish their own righteousness; therefore they were not subject to the righteousness of God. That brought them down.
For you are the glory of their strength, and in your good pleasure our horn shall be exalted. For you are the glory of their strength,
and in your well-beloved Christ our horn is exalted. From him we have the power to become sons of God. For our taking-up is the Lord's
and the Holy One's of Israel, our king. For our taking-up is the Lord's, and the Holy One's of Israel, our king. He took our nature upon himself
when he became incarnate. THEN YOU SPOKE IN A VISION TO YOUR SONS. Then you spoke in sight to your sons. You made your
If they profane my justices and do not keep my commandments. But if his children, who are called sons of the bridegroom,
forsake my law, and do not walk in my judgments, and break my statutes, and do not keep my commandments,
I will visit their iniquities with the rod, and their sins with stripes. Then I will punish their wrongdoing with the rod, and their sins
with scourges. But my mercy I will not scatter away from him, nor will I do harm in my truth. But my mercy I will not remove from him,
nor will I harm him in my truth. The truth of my promise does not harm him,
because I promised him mercy in his children. Nor will I profane my covenant, and what proceeds from my lips I will not make void.
Nor will I profane my covenant, and what I speak, that I will not undo. Once I have sworn by my holy one.
Once I swore that I would make it good in my holy Son, when I gave him up to death for the sins of all.
If I lie to David, his seed shall remain forever. I will not become a liar to David; his seed endures forever.
His seed are the good, from whom the harvest grows, whose reapers are the angels. And his throne is like the sun in my sight.
And his throne will be like the sun in my sight. The righteous are his throne; on them he sits. They will shine in the future kingdom like the sun.
And like the full moon forever. And like an ever-full moon. In soul they will become perfect like the sun,
in flesh like the moon: not like this waning moon, but like the one that is always full. And a faithful witness in heaven.
And such a moon, which is forever a faithful witness against all those who deny the resurrection of the flesh.
But you have rejected and despised, and put off your anointed. Where has all that gone which you promised him?
Contrary to your promises you have thrust away, and dishonored, and put off your anointed one.
If you promised it to David, from whom our Christ came, you have broken it for him. He was thrust from the kingdom by his own son
and driven into flight, and in that flight he was dishonored by the son of Gemini. But our Christ you have only put off.
You have put him off, not taken him away. What about that other one? You have overturned the covenant of your servant. You have entirely set aside
and torn up your servant's covenant. Where is the old covenant of the Jews, under which David lived? Where do they now have the land of promise?
Where is their kingdom? Where is sacrifice, where is priesthood? You have profaned his sanctuary on earth. You have desecrated his temple on earth
and left it idle, for from now on no one may keep the sabbath and sacrifice cattle. You have destroyed all his walls.
You tore down all his fortifications, in which he was to have his strength. You have made his strongholds a terror.
The very strongholds from which courage should have come, you made into a cause of fear for them. All who pass along the way have plundered him.
All who travel along the way have torn him to pieces. By the Romans the first David was scattered among all the nations.
What is the reproach? "Because they have reproached the change of your Christ." That they reproach us with the change of your anointed one,
which they did not recognize as being from earth to heaven, from temporal life to eternal life, from the Jews to the Gentiles; instead they thought it was destruction.
That led them astray. But Christ, rising from the dead, dies no more; death shall no longer have dominion over him. He would give that change to them as well, if they wished.
Of them it is written: "For there is no change for them, and they have not feared God." Blessed be the Lord forever.
May the Lord be praised forever. So be it, so be it. May it be so. Here ends the second sermon, delivered at the vigils of Saint Cyprian.
Here is the end of this psalm, which was preached at two matins of Saint Cyprian.
A PRAYER OF MOSES, THE SERVANT OF GOD. Although Moses did not write this psalm, yet
the title is there so that it may be all the more acceptable to us [?]. LORD, YOU HAVE BECOME OUR REFUGE from generation to generation.
Lord, you have become a refuge for us, in generation and in generation: in the old one and in the new one.
Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world were formed, from age to age, that is, from eternity to eternity, you are God.
Before the mountains came to be, which are the angels, and before the earth came to be, which is human beings, and the world itself
in which both of them are, you exist before. From eternity to eternity you are. Do not turn man away into lowliness.
You do not turn man away down into lowliness; do not let him be desirous of what is low rather than of what is high.
And you said: Be converted, sons of men. And so you commanded; you said: Turn, you sons of men.
Help us toward what you commanded. For a thousand years before your eyes are like yesterday, which has passed.
This conversion is needed because before your eyes the ten hundred years that the people of old before the Flood nearly lived out
are as short as yesterday, which has passed. And like a watch in the night. And as short as a watch,
which according to the Romans is no more than three hours, that is, the fourth part of the night. If you wish to interpret mille according to custom as 'thousand' [dûsent],
then understand that this same word has been corrupted from another. The Romans say colloquially, for decies centum ('ten hundred'), 'dêscent';
in its place we say 'dûsent' [thousand]. Likewise they also say [?] 'eînhunt' 'unzent', 'ducent', 'tercent';
in their place we say 'one hundred', 'two hundred', 'three hundred'. Things that are counted as nothing, such will their years be. What you consider as nothing,
that is their years, even when they are most numerous. In the morning, that is, at first, may it pass like grass; in the morning may it flourish.
May their life at first pass like grass; may their life also blossom at first. And may it perish in the evening.
And after that may it be lost. May it fall: may it plunge into death. May it harden: may it grow stiff in the corpse.
And may it wither: and may it dry up in the ashes. For we have failed in your anger, and in your fury we have been troubled.
how insignificant the good is that is promised in the Old Testament, where there is the shadow of things to come, and that they therefore lightly give up their hope in such things.
And if Moses named earthly things to them, it was so that they might learn from Christ to understand heavenly things. And if it should also say:
"Make your right hand thus known, and those fettered in heart in wisdom," then it has the same meaning. Then Moses prays further
that Christ may thus become known to us, and his teachers, who are constrained in their hearts, so that they may draw us to spiritual understanding.
Turn, Lord, somewhat, and be entreated on behalf of your servants. Be turned somewhat, Lord, back here to us,
away from your anger, in which you are turned away, and be entreated for mercy on behalf of your servants.
Is this not the prayer of Moses in Exodus: BE APPEASED OVER THE WICKEDNESS OF YOUR PEOPLE? And if it says, "Turn, Lord, how long,"
or "until when," that again means "somewhat" or "to some extent," indefinitely, not as a question. Such is the prayer:
Spare somewhat, Lord, the martyrs, who are to endure many evils in the New Testament because they do not care for the things promised in the Old Testament.
Spare them somewhat, lest, overcome, they begin to flee from you. Yet let them not be without all distress, so that their crown does not escape them.
We have been filled in the morning with your mercy, and we have rejoiced and been delighted in all our days. Openly we are filled with your grace,
and for that we are gladdened, and delighted in all our days. That we shall openly see Christ in the flesh, that is our joy
all our days. We have been glad for the days in which you humbled us, the years in which we saw evils. We have also become glad because of the days
in which you made us humble, and because of the years in which we saw grievous things. Then they were grievous, now they are dear,
because we have been bettered by them. Look upon your servants, that is, the Jews, and upon your works. Look on your servants
and on your works. Those who are your servants are also your works. And direct their sons.
And direct their sons: if the forebears are scattered, let them nevertheless be converted at the end of the world. And let the splendour of the Lord our God be upon us.
And let the brightness of our God be over us. Let his face be shown to us. And direct the works of our hands over us.
And direct the work of our hands over us, so that we do not do it for worldly thanks, for then it is crooked.
And direct the work of our hands. And since all works look to the one work of charity, direct that one work.
Some books do not have the last verse. Of what does the name of Moses remind us here?
Only that his law and the whole Old Testament is written under a veil, and we therefore pray Christ to take away the veil.
David teaches us this prayer thus: UNVEIL MY EYES. "Uncover my eyes," he said. AND I WILL CONSIDER THE WONDERS OF YOUR LAW.
And then I will perceive wonders from your law. What wonders? Hidden mysteries, of which the Holy Spirit is the revealer.
PRAISE OF A SONG OF DAVID.

against those whom he displeased, who said: "No, but he leads the crowds astray." What is this strength? Nothing other than humility,
with which he endured them. Pride, its opposite, is weakness. And he has girded himself. And he was girded. He had before him,
when he hung on the cross, mockers who said to him: "Hail, King of the Jews." There he showed himself girded.
There he showed himself strong and ready to endure the wicked. For he has established the world, which shall not be moved.
By doing this he made the holy Church firm, which from now on stands steadfast and will not be moved. From now on it stands in faith.
It may be shaken; it will not be torn up. Your throne has been prepared since then. From then on, flesh is your seat. In the sixth age of the world
you came; since then you have sat in the hearts of the faithful. You are from everlasting. Before that, and before all time, you are. Forever and ever you are. The floods have lifted up, O Lord,
the floods have lifted up their voice. The rivers, Lord, the rivers raised up their voice. When the Holy Spirit came,
the apostles became very loud in their preaching. The floods have lifted up their waves, at the voices of many waters.
After them came other waters, which raised up their waves, meaning the boldness they had
from the roar of many waters. The more of them there were, the bolder they became. Wonderful are the surges of the sea.
From this the anger of worldly people became wonderful. From what? From the voices of many waters. How wonderful?
So wonderful that no one can count the host of martyrs who lay slain by that wrath. And what then? The Lord on high is wonderful.
The Lord was also wonderful in those very high and very powerful kings who did this.
Where does this appear? Your testimonies have become exceedingly credible. Your testimonies became very credible.
They became credible to the kings themselves, just as to the others. As it says: "In me you shall have peace."
"In the world you shall have distress. But take courage: I have overcome the world." What comes of this?
Holiness befits your house, O Lord, for length of days. Holiness befits your Church in eternity.
Its holiness appears in the other world. There it befits it, because there it will not be darkened.

A PSALM OF DAVID HIMSELF, FOR THE FOURTH DAY OF THE WEEK. A psalm to Christ for Wednesday. On that day the lights of heaven were made, which since then have shone on the good and the wicked. They stand fixed in the firmament
of heaven. So also stand those whose way of life is in heaven. And just as the lights do not care what is done on earth
and do not leave their courses because of it, so too those who are heavenly do not, because of earthly people,
fail to keep up [?] their way of life. Whatever is done to them or to others, they bear it with patience. Whoever loses that patience
falls from heaven. This psalm shows that. The Lord is the God of vengeance; the God of vengeance has acted freely.
God is the lord of vengeance, because he leaves nothing unavenged. The God of vengeance acted boldly when he came "among men."
As it says: "He was teaching them as one having authority, not as their scribes and Pharisees." Those whom he saw doing evil,
he rebuked boldly, because he is "the God of vengeances," and he wanted them to be spared "vengeance." "Be exalted, you who judge the earth."
Be exalted "in the resurrection," you who bring earthly men to judgment. Go boldly to heaven, you who were bold on earth.
"Render retribution to the proud." Repay the proud; forgive the humble. The proud who slew you were struck with terror
by the miracles of the apostles, and, having become humble, they said to them: "What shall we do, men and brothers?" Then they heard from Peter:
"Do penance, and let each one of you be baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ."
Forgive them; forgive them the greatest debts. What is the debt? "They shed their own price."
What do you grant them in return "through forgiveness"? "Let them drink their own price." So your prayer has reached them, the prayer you made on the cross…
…"Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." "How long shall sinners, O Lord, how long shall sinners glory?"
The Holy Spirit himself speaks together with men and asks what they have to ask: How long, Lord, will sinners boast?
How long? "They will utter and speak iniquity; all who work injustice will speak." Sinners say and speak injustice.
All who do it speak it. They say: God does not know our injustice. Why do they say that, except that God bears with them
and lets them live? They hide from the police officer so that he will not catch them, but they do not hide from God,
because they do not think that he is present at their wrongdoing. They say: Since our wrongs displease judges,
the laws, emperors and prison officers, whom we flee, would we be any less able to escape him…
…if it displeased him, or if he knew of it beforehand? "Your people, O Lord, they have humbled, and your inheritance they have afflicted."
By speaking this way they humbled your people, who could not hear it without pain, and with it they troubled your inheritance,
that is, your faithful. "They slew the widow and the stranger, and they killed the orphans." They slew widows and strangers and orphans.
Of these it is written: "You shall not harm the pilgrim and the stranger." "And they said: The Lord will not see." And they said:
God does not see this. "Nor will the God of Jacob understand." Nor does the God of Jacob know it. "Understand, you foolish among the people,
and you fools, be wise at last." Take heed, you unwise among the people, and you fools, come to your senses at last.
"He who planted the ear, shall he not hear?" He who created the ear, does he not hear? "Or he who formed the eye, does he not…
…see?" Or he who made the eye, does he not see? Does he himself not have what he gave to others? "He who chastises the nations, shall he not rebuke?"
He who sent the prophets out beforehand "to chasten the nations," when he comes himself, shall he not then "rebuke"? What they did, shall he not do that?
Who teaches man knowledge? He makes another know; does he himself not know? The Lord knows the thoughts of men, that they are vain.
God knows the thoughts of men; he knows that they are vain. They do not know that his are right.
But he knows that theirs are vain. There are, however, some who know his thoughts; they are called friends of God.
Blessed is the man whom you instruct, O Lord, and teach out of your law. Blessed is the man whom you, Lord, teach,
and to whom you give teaching from your law. Which teaching? That you may calm him from the evil days. That you may make him gentle
and quiet him in the evil days, such as are those in which the wicked prosper. Until a pit is dug for the sinner. That he may restrain himself,
and that it may not weigh on him, until a pit is dug for the sinner, into which he falls and never stands up again.
What is the pit? It is his prosperity. It gives him pride, and through it he falls.
That comes from the hidden ordering of God. Whoever is taught this by him does not say to God: Why do the wicked reign
and the good are oppressed? For the Lord will not cast off his people. For God does not thrust his people away from him on that account.
What does he do, then? He exercises them; he does not cast them off. He improves them by means of the wicked, hardens them, makes them patient
and steadfast. And he will not forsake his inheritance. And he does not abandon his inheritance because of the others' wickedness. Those to whom he wishes to give the inheritance,
he scourges; the others he lets do what they want. Until justice is turned into judgment. Be righteous in the meantime,
and do not let God's ordering displease you until your justice is turned into judgment, until you sit together with him to judge,
just as the apostles too were first just and afterward become judges. And all who hold it are upright of heart.
Those who do this, who hold fast to justice, have a straight heart, not a crooked one.
Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? Or who will stand with me against the workers of iniquity? Who will come to help me against the malicious?
Or who will stand by me against those who act unjustly? They at once disparage my way of life
if they see me living in the Christian manner, with reproaches like this: Why do you not do what others do?
You alone are a Christian. Ecstasy has carried you off with Paul into the third heaven. Unless the Lord had helped me, almost,
that is, nearly, my soul would have dwelt in hell. If God did not help me, I could easily be led astray by such words
and my soul would go to hell. Among such people I would not be saved if God did not do it. If I said: My foot is moved,
your mercy, O Lord, helped me. If in humility I confessed my sins and said: My foot has slipped,
then your mercy, God, always helped me. According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, your consolations have gladdened my soul.
As many as the pains that were upon me, so many were the consolations that gladdened my soul.
To whom I swore thus in my anger, and so threatened: they shall not come into my rest. That is: they shall not become blessed.
There all good is denied to them. This psalm begins in joy and ends in sorrow.
A SONG OF DAVID WHEN THE HOUSE WAS BEING BUILT AFTER THE CAPTIVITY. Thus David sang when the house was built after the exile.
Which house is this? Once a house was built after the exile, when Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, having returned from the Babylonian captivity,
rebuilt Solomon's house, which had been destroyed by the Chaldeans. Does this psalm speak of that? No.
It speaks of holy Church, which is the house of God: how it was built with the new song of faith, hope and charity
after the captivity of unbelief. SING TO THE LORD A NEW SONG. Sing to the Lord, all the earth. Sing to the Lord a new song.
Let all the earth sing it to him. Love is the new song, because it is the new commandment. All the earth is holy Church. It is the house of God,
and it is built with charity. In this building all the stones become one stone. How does that happen? In the unity of the Spirit, in the bond of peace. Sing
to the Lord. Sing to the Lord. Sing a new song; in this way you build a new house. Bless his name.
Praise his name. How? Announce well his salvation from day to day. Make his Savior, Christ, well known
from day to day, so that he may become ever better and better known. Announce his glory among the nations,
his wonders among all peoples. Make known his glory among the nations, and his wonders among all people.
In this way make him well known, and in this way build him a wide house. For the Lord is great and exceedingly to be praised,
terrible above all gods. For he is a mighty Lord, and greatly to be praised, and terrible above all gods.
What then are we to believe about them? For all the gods of the nations are demons. That is, all the gods of the heathen peoples
are devils. Those whom error invented, they are demons. But the Lord made the heavens. But the Lord made the heavens,
from which he cast them down; so mighty is he. Confession and beauty are in his sight. Confession and beauty are before him.
Let the confession of sins go first; then beauty follows at once. When you have washed yourself clean, you are beautiful before him.
Holiness and magnificence are in his sanctification. Holiness first, and great works afterwards, are in his sanctification.
His sanctification has this order: it brings you from holiness to magnificence. If you wish to be magnificent in signs and miracles first,
before you become holy, that cannot happen. Bring to the Lord, O families of the nations, bring to the Lord glory and honor.
You peoples, bring to the Lord glory and honor. Bring them to him, [?] not to yourselves, nor to other people.
Bring to the Lord glory for his name. Bring to him, in praise, glory for his name; say: NOT TO US, O LORD, NOT
TO US, BUT TO YOUR NAME GIVE GLORY. Take up sacrifices and enter into his courts. Take offerings that are fitting for him.
THE LORD HAS REIGNED. After his resurrection Christ reigns, because then those were sent out who made his kingdom known to the people.
Let the peoples be angry. The people are angered at this, because their idols are to be destroyed. Or they are angry with themselves for their sins
and do penance. You who sit upon the cherubim, let the earth be moved. You who reach above all the fullness of knowledge, to you I say: LET THE EARTH BE MOVED.
Either to persecution, so that the martyrs may be crowned, or to penance, so that they themselves may be saved. What is the fullness of knowledge?
Of knowledge [the fullness] is charity. Have charity; then you reach to the cherubim. The Lord in Zion is great and exalted above all peoples.
Zion is the Church. Be in the Church; then God is great and exalted in you. Be also yourself Zion.
Be a contemplator of the divine light; then you will be illuminated, and from that illumination God becomes great and exalted in you in all virtues, above all the people
who were angry with him over their idols. Let them confess your great name. Let them acknowledge your great name.
Those who at first would not acknowledge him when he was small, because he had not yet come far, they will acknowledge him as great
when he becomes known everywhere. Why? Because it is terrible and holy. Because he is terrible and holy. Terrible
because he is the judge; holy because he is God. And the honor of the king loves judgment. And because the king's honor loves judgment,
therefore let everyone be just, because he loves judgment. You have prepared equity. You prepared right. Where?
Hear this. You have done judgment and justice in Jacob. In the holy Church you did judgment and right.
She did not take it from herself; you taught her both. Let everyone learn to do judgment. How?
By discerning between good and evil. But justice, how? That he turn away from evil and do good. Exalt the Lord our God.
Exalt the Lord our God; magnify him from whom we received justice, so that we may be justified.
And worship the footstool of his feet, for it is holy. And worship his footstool, because it is holy. The earth is the footstool of his feet.
He took earth from earth, flesh from the flesh of Mary. In that very flesh he walked here; that very flesh he gave us to eat; we must worship it
when we eat it, because it is a sacrament, and in a sacrament there is always a spiritual meaning. The footstool of his feet may also mean
the stability of his divinity. Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among those who call upon his name; they called upon the Lord, and he
heard them. Let us worship the footstool of his feet earnestly and gladly, so that he may hear us.
For Moses and Aaron, two of his priests, and Samuel, one of those who prayed to him, prayed to him, and he heard them.
Were there no more of them whom he heard? There was an infinite multitude of them, on whose behalf these three are named.
Was Moses a priest? He interceded for his people as priests do; therefore he is counted among them here.
He spoke to them in the pillar of cloud. He spoke to them out of the pillar of cloud. That was a figure.
That is what an unrighteous heart says, such as belongs to the man who takes offence at God's will and so quarrels with him: GOD, WHAT HAVE I DONE TO YOU?
WHAT HAVE I COMMITTED? WHAT HAVE I DESERVED? I do not wish to be his companion, because with a perverse heart he considers himself just
and God unjust. The wicked one who turned away from me I did not know, that is, I did not approve. The heretic who turned to faithlessness I did not fol-
-low. Whoever secretly slandered his neighbour, him I persecuted. The man who backbit another I hunted down and persecuted,
because the persecution by which one hastens to make the man better is good. With the proud eye and the insatiable heart, with him I did not eat.
With the proud man, and with the one who out of envy cannot be sated by the woes of others, I did not eat. All the proud are envious,
and they are fed by the misfortunes of others, yet not satisfied. Their company is to be fled. My eyes are on the faithful of the earth,
that they may sit with me. My eyes are turned toward the faithful inhabitants of the earth. I desire their fellowship. For what purpose?
That they may sit with me to judge. As one of them said: DO YOU NOT KNOW THAT WE SHALL JUDGE ANGELS?
He who walked in the undefiled way ministered to me. Going in the unspotted way, he served me. Who is that?
None other than the faithful preacher of the gospel, who does not seek his own things but those of Jesus Christ. He who acts with pride shall not dwell in the midst of my house.
He who is proud does not dwell in my heart. I have one heart together with the humble; I have a heart that recoils from the proud.
He who speaks unjust things did not go straight in the sight of my eyes. Speaking wrong, he went astray before me.
Wherever he saw me, there he shied away; he fled from there. In the morning, that is, in the beginning, I killed all the sinners of the earth,
so that I might destroy from the city of the Lord all who work iniquity. In the beginning I slew all the sinners of the earth.
At the beginning of temptation I slew all the tempting demons, so that I might drive them out of my soul, which is the Lord's city
and his dwelling. Demons are rightly called sinners of the earth and workers of iniquity, because they cause
earthly people to sin and to act wickedly. But they are slain in their works by those who resist them right at the onset of temptation
and drive them away by cursing them. 'In the mornings' may also be understood as the day of judgment, as it says: JUDGE NOTHING BEFORE THE TIME,
UNTIL THE LORD COMES, WHO WILL BRING TO LIGHT THE HIDDEN THINGS OF DARKNESS AND WILL MAKE MANIFEST THE COUNSELS OF HEARTS. Now it is night;
now no one knows another. Then it will be seen who each one is; then it is morning; then all who work iniquity will be driven out of the city of the Lord.
THE PRAYER OF THE POOR MAN WHEN HE IS IN ANGUISH AND POURS OUT HIS PRAYER BEFORE THE LORD. This is a poor man's prayer when he is in distress
and then implores God about it. For this reason, in some places it applies to Christ, who for our sake became poor,
and to his bride, holy Church, which is one with him in one flesh and in one voice, and to each of his faithful who is in need.
LORD, HEAR MY PRAYER, AND LET MY CRY COME TO YOU. Lord Father, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to
[?] you. May my prayer be so loud that it comes to you. Ne avertas faciem tuam a me: Do not turn your face away from me.
Do not turn it away from those who are poor and are my members. In quacumque die tribulor, inclina ad me aurem tuam: On whatever day I am in distress, incline your ear to me.
Whenever I come into distress, incline your ear to me. I am in distress down below, but you are up above.
On whichever side there is need, help me on that side. In quacumque die invocavero te, velociter exaudi me: On whatever day I call upon you, hear me quickly. In this generation, in the second,
and in the third, and in whichever one I call upon you, hear me quickly, for I ask for what you gladly give.
What is that? Nothing other than the kingdom of heaven. Do as you promised when you said: "While you are still speaking, I will say:
'Here I am.'" Quia defecerunt sicut fumus dies mei: For my days have vanished like smoke. Therefore hear me soon, for my days have passed away like smoke.
Adam earned such days. Want and poverty lie upon me. Et ossa mea sicut in frixorio confrixa sunt: And my bones are fried as in a frying pan.
And my bones are roasted as if in a pan. They smolder for fear of the eternal fire.
These words belong to the penitent. But they may also be Christ's, in that he calls his strong ones bones, as the apostles are,
for in them he is burned, according to these words: "Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?" Love causes the frying.
Percussum est sicut faenum et aruit cor meum: My heart is struck down like hay and has withered. My heart is struck, and so it dried up like hay. Hay dries from being cut.
I have become like hay because of sins that strike me down. Why is that? Quia oblitus sum manducare panem meum: Because I forgot to eat my bread.
Because I did not remember to eat my bread. God's commandment is the bread of the soul; against it I ate what was forbidden.
Therefore it has rightly befallen me. A voce gemitus mei adhaeserunt ossa mea carni meae: At the sound of my groaning my bones have cleaved to my flesh. At the sound of my sighing
my bones cleaved to my flesh. By sighing I obtained this from God: that we who are firm should cling to the infirm,
and we who are strong to the weak. They would not sigh over their infirmity, so I sighed for them.
As it says: "For we who are firm ought to bear the infirmity of the weak." Similis factus sum pellicano solitudinis: I have become like a pelican of the wilderness.
From sighing and from grief I am as lean as the pelican that flies in Egypt, in the wildernesses of the river Nile, of which the naturalists say
that it digests nothing of what it swallows, no more than the cormorant does here in these lakes.

Factus sum sicut nycticorax in parietinis, that is, in domicilio: I have become like the night raven among ruined walls, that is, in a dwelling. I have also become like the night raven in the ruined houses, where it is undisturbed,
because no human being is there. Instead of nycticorax, some understand bubo or noctua or onocrotalus,
that is, the eagle-owl or the owl or the bittern. Vigilavi et factus sum sicut passer singularis in tecto: I have kept watch and have become like a solitary sparrow on the roof.
I kept watch and have become like the sparrow that stays alone in the house, for other birds fly away;
the sparrow stays at home. These three birds stand for three ways of life of the saints. The pelican stands for hermits.
they turned to the faith: first three thousand, after that five thousand. So that they too become made solid into stones.
And the nations shall fear your name, O Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory. Therefore, after that, all peoples too fear your name,
and all kings your glory, and the Church spreads itself over everything. Why is that? Because the Lord shall build up Zion.
For the Lord himself builds it. And he shall be seen in his glory. And when the time for that comes, he shall be seen in glory
who before was seen in weakness. He has regarded the prayer of the humble, and has not despised their petition. On the prayer of the humble
he looked, and he did not reject their entreaty. Since that is so, let all be humble in this building,
and let all pray. Let these things be written for another generation. Let these words, these prophecies, be written for another generation,
when the New Testament comes, so that they may be more useful to that generation than to the earlier one, and that it may be a memorial from generation to generation.
And the people that shall be created shall praise the Lord. And then the people that becomes a new creature in baptism praises God. For he has looked forth from his holy heaven;
the Lord has looked from heaven upon the earth. That will happen because the Lord looked down here; from heaven he looked to earth;
from on high he came to the humble. Why? That he might hear the groans of those in fetters. That he might hear the sighing of the oppressed.
The fear and discipline of God are the fetters whose prisoners he hears. And that he might set free the sons of the slain. And he also came
so that he might unbind the sons of the slain. Those who were slain by the devil's deceit — we are their sons.
He unbinds us because he gives us remission of sins. That the name of the Lord may be proclaimed in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem.
That God's name may be made known by the apostles in the Church, and his praise in Jerusalem — that is again the Church.
When the peoples gather together into one, and the kingdoms, to serve the Lord. That peoples and kingdoms, coming together, serve God
and become his catholic Church. She answered him in the way of his strength. Then Jerusalem answered him
on the way of her strength, which is Christ. She responded to his calling with good works, with his help.
But the former Jerusalem answered him with evil works. Therefore she heard: BEHOLD, YOUR HOUSE SHALL BE LEFT TO YOU DE-
SERTED. Declare to me the fewness of my days. Make known to me, says the Church, the fewness of my days.
Let me hear: BEHOLD, I AM WITH YOU ALL DAYS, EVEN TO THE END OF THE WORLD.
Although that span is small compared with eternity, it still gladdens me that I do not pass away before then, and that the heretics are lying
who promise me otherwise. Do not call me back in the midst of my days. Do not turn me back at the half part of my days,
as they suppose. Do not let them be fewer than you have spoken. Your years are for ever and ever.
For ever and ever are your years. Compared with yours, mine are few. In the beginning, O Lord, you founded the earth.
and the heavens are the works of your hands. They will perish, but you remain. In the beginning you founded the earth,
and the heavens are your handiwork. Though they are so, they will pass away. You stand firm, and are what you are.
And all of them will grow old like a garment, and like a covering you will change them, and they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will not fail.
And they will all grow old like clothing, and you will change them, and they will undergo the change. But you are always the same,
and your years do not pass away. In the Flood the heavens nearest the earth were destroyed, the ones in which the birds are. There are also higher heavens,
which are called the heavens of heavens. Whether these are to be destroyed by fire together with those,
or only those and not these, or what change is to happen to them, is a difficult dispute among the learned.
Or what is written here about the heavens can be understood of the saints and the righteous,
in whom God thunders with commandments, flashes with miracles, and rains upon the earth with the wisdom of tru-
-th, of whom it says: THE HEAVENS DECLARE THE GLORY OF GOD. Of them this is well understood: AND ALL WILL GROW OLD LIKE A GARMENT.
AND LIKE A COVERING YOU WILL CHANGE THEM, AND THEY WILL BE CHANGED. What are their bodies but the garments and coverings of the soul?
In these they will be changed, as the apostle says: AND THE DEAD WILL RISE INCORRUPT, AND WE SHALL BE CHANGED.
How shall we be changed? It is sown a natural body; it will rise a spiritual body. It is sown mortal; it will rise immortal. It is sown corruptible;
it will rise incorruptible. Their bodies too are heavens, because they carry God, according to the words of Paul:
GLORIFY AND BEAR GOD IN YOUR BODY. Such heavens grow old so that they may be renewed.
The children of your servants will dwell, that is, in your years. In your eternal years the children of the apostles dwell. And their seed will be directed forever.
And their offspring will be directed into eternity, where all things move in their proper order. The beginning of this psalm is words of groaning; the end is words of consolation.
BLESS THE LORD, O MY SOUL. My soul, give thanks to God. And all that is within me, bless his holy name.
And let all that is in me give thanks to his holy name. Let the reason that is in it, and all its thoughts, praise him. Bless the Lord, O my soul,
and do not forget all his rewards. Thank him, and do not forget any of his reward. You earned evil things; he gave you good things,
and still gives them, as is written further on: Who is merciful to all your iniquities, who heals all your diseases. Who to all your wrongs shows mer-
-cy, who heals all your sicknesses. Who redeems your life from destruction. Who redeems your life from perdition.
Who crowns you with compassion and mercy. Who crowns you with pity and with mercy. 'Corona' (crown) means an ornament of the head,
that is, the adornment of the head, as we see on kings. Who satisfies your desire with good things.
Who fulfills your desire with good, that is, who fills you with good. Your youth will be renewed like the eagle's.
He has not forgotten that we are dust. Those who could have been noble have become so lowly through sin. "Man, his days are like grass."
Man is like hay. His days are like hay. "As the flower of the field, so shall he flourish." Like the flower there in the field,
so he blooms and withers; so short-lived is he. "For the spirit shall pass away in him, and he shall not remain, and he shall no longer know his place."
For his spirit, which is in him, departs, and he does not remain here, nor does he ever return here again. If he is to be blessed after he has gone from here,
that comes through the grace of him who took on himself grass, to make gold out of it. "But the mercy of the Lord is from age to age, and for ever, upon those who fear him."
But God's grace is upon those who fear him, from the beginning of this world, and from then on into the world to come.
Here, where it says "from age" (a saeculo), many supposed, as Cassiodorus says, that grace was promised to Adam, because others came into being in the world (in saeculo);

he came into being from the beginning of the world (a saeculo). "And his righteousness is upon children's children, upon those who keep his covenant and are mindful of his commandments, to do them." And his righteousness
shows, that is, in our sons' sons; these are works and the rewards of works. And it shows in those who keep his covenant
and are mindful of his commandments so that they fulfil them. His covenant (testamentum) is his commandments.
They all consist in charity, and we must be mindful of them. "The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven, and his kingdom shall rule over all."
The Lord prepared his throne in heaven, at the right hand of the Father, and his kingdom rules over them all. "Bless
the Lord, all you his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word, hearkening to the voice of his words." Praise God, all his angels, mighty in power,
you who do his word to hear, that is, to fulfil the voice of his words. "Bless the Lord, all you his hosts,
his ministers who do his will." Praise the Lord, all his hosts, his servants,
you who fulfil his will. "Bless the Lord, all his works." Let all his works praise him. "In every place of his dominion,
bless the Lord, O my soul." In all the places where his power is, there praise God, my soul.
His power is everywhere; praise him everywhere, not only within the enclosures of the church but also outside its enclosures.
"BLESS THE LORD, O MY SOUL." My soul, praise the Lord for the beautiful things that this psalm shows.
"O Lord my God, you are magnified exceedingly." O Lord my God, you are greatly magnified. You have shown yourself great
to those who did not know your greatness before. "You have put on confession and beauty." You have clothed yourself in confession and adornment,
because your church put on these two. At first she was dark, before she began to confess her sins,
but by confessing she was made white. Her putting on is your putting on. "Clothed with light as with a garment." Covered with light
as with a garment. Her garment is your garment; that is the light of faith. "Stretching out the heaven like a skin."
Stretching out the heaven as a hide is stretched. After animals die, their hides are stretched.
And they fear because of the voice of your thunder, your threat, which is this: UNLESS YOU DO PENANCE,
YOU WILL ALL PERISH TOGETHER. The mountains rise up and the plains go down, to the place which you founded for them. So the preachers raise themselves up, and the peoples
let themselves down, as far as the place of your Church, which you made firm for them, because it will not be moved for ever and ever.
You have set them a boundary which they shall not pass over, nor shall they turn back to cover the earth. You set a boundary in the catholic faith, which they do not step beyond,
nor do they turn back again to cover the earth, that is, to renew their sins and to become unbelieving again.
You who send forth springs in the valleys. You who let the springs flow out in the valleys: you give the humble the knowledge of doctrine.
Between the mountains the waters will pass. In the midst of the mountains the waters flow away. The teaching of the apostles is common to all.
"The midst" means what is common. All the beasts of the forest will drink. From it all the nations drink. The wild asses will wait in their thirst.
The Jews wait in their thirst until Elijah and Enoch come. Above them the birds of the sky will dwell; from among the rocks they will give voice.
Above them sit the spiritual ones: the holy souls of the bishops take care of them. They speak out of stones:
what they have from the prophets and apostles, not from Plato, that is what they teach. Watering the mountains from his upper places.
But you water the apostles from heaven. Just as those others have it from the apostles, so the apostles in turn have it from you,
for you fill them with the Holy Spirit. The earth will be satisfied with the fruit of your works. With the increase of your works
the earth becomes satisfied. That is the earth that is satisfied with the teaching which you rain down from heaven.
Bringing forth hay for the cattle. Bearing hay for the cattle, as it says: YOU SHALL NOT MUZZLE THE MOUTH OF THE OX THAT TREADS OUT THE GRAIN.
And plants for the service of men. And plants for the service of men: giving provision to those who are ministers of the word of God,
whom he just now called cattle. That you may bring forth bread from the earth. That you, God the Father, thus reveal Christ out of the earth, out of earthen vessels,
in which the apostles held the treasure of doctrine. And wine gladdens the heart of man. And wine then gladdens the heart of man.
Spiritual drunkenness gives him love of heavenly things. Or the fill of the Lord's body and blood makes them glad.
That it may make the face cheerful with oil, that is, with brightness. That this fill may make his face cheerful with radiance,
so that some grace of God may shine openly in him: either of healings, or of tongues, or of prophecy, or of some other charism.
For it says: TO EACH ONE IS GIVEN THE MANIFESTATION OF THE SPIRIT FOR THE COMMON GOOD. And that bread may strengthen the heart of man. And bread,
that is, the soul's nourishment, may strengthen his heart. The trees of the field will be satisfied. With this grace, that is, with bread, wine and oil,
the common people of the nations become satisfied, that is, the ordinary ones. And the cedars of Lebanon. So the mighty also become satisfied, who stand above others,
as the cedars that grow on Lebanon stand above other trees. Are they all satisfied? No. Those which he planted.
The Lord shall rejoice in his works. The Lord rejoices in his own works, not in those of man, because those are evil.
Who looks upon the earth and makes it tremble. He who looks upon man and makes him tremble. Whomever he looks upon in this way,
upon him he rests. As he himself said: Upon whom does my spirit rest? Upon the humble and the quiet and the one who trembles at my words.
Who touches the mountains and they shall smoke. He who strikes proud men and pricks them to penance, and once struck in this way they smoke,
because then they lament their sins. I will sing to the Lord in my life; I will sing psalms to my God as long as I exist. I sing to the Lord as long as I live,
because here I have hope. I will also sing to him for as long as I am in eternity, where there is no other work except the praise of God.
Let my speech be pleasing to him; but I shall delight in the Lord. May my speech be pleasing to him; my delight is in him.
I make myself known to him, who knows; may he make himself known to me, who do not know. Let my confession be sweet to him; his grace is sweet to me.
That is mutual delight. Let sinners fail from the earth. Let sinners slip away from earthly desire. And the unrighteous, so that they may not be.
And let the unrighteous perish, so that they may not be, that is, may not be unrighteous. Then he sends forth his spirit for their renewal. Be-
-nedic anima mea dominum ("Bless the Lord, O my soul"). Praise the Lord, my soul. That was the beginning of the psalm; let it also be the ending.
Alleluia is Hebrew; in Latin it means "Praise the Lord." Give praise to the Lord. That is the same thing.
It says "Praise God," because here "confession" refers to praise. And call upon his name. And so, when it is time, come and call upon him.
Proclaim his works among the nations. Make known his works among the peoples. This is spoken to the apostles and to the evangelists.
Sing to him. Sing to him: that is, in words. And play psalms to him. And touch the strings for him:
that is, in deeds. Praise him in both of these. Tell all his wonders. Recount all his wonders.
Even if you are not able to, do not lack the will. Be praised in his holy name. Be praised in his name:
it is his power that makes you worthy of praise, not your own. Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
Let the hearts of those who seek God be glad; let them be without bitter zeal. Seek the Lord and be strengthened. Seek God and be strengthened.
Draw near to him in such a way that you are first enlightened, so you can see what is to be done, and afterwards strengthened,
so that you do not grow weary in doing it. Seek his face always. Always seek his presence. You have found him by faith;
seek him by sight. When you see him face to face, even then seek him without end, because you will love him without end.
Remember the wonders that he did. Remember the wonders that he did in the parting of the Red Sea
and in turning back the Jordan. His portents. Remember the portents he showed in the plagues of Egypt. For portents
are things that never happened before. And the judgments of his mouth. And remember the judgments of his mouth, which he taught to Moses.
and worshipped the graven image. Horeb means "skull" (calvaria). On that Calvary they worshipped an idol; on the other they slew Christ. And they changed their glory
into the likeness of a calf that eats hay. And their glory, which was in God, they exchanged for the image of the beast
that lives on hay. They forgot God who saved them, who did great things in Egypt, wonders in the land of Ham,
terrible things in the Red Sea. They forgot God who saved them, who did mighty works in Egypt, wonders in the land of Ham,
terrible things in the Red Sea. And he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen one stood in the breach before him,
And then he said that he would destroy them, if Moses his chosen one had not stood before him in the breach,
in the plague, to turn away his wrath, lest he destroy them. He stood so firmly that he turned away His wrath, so that He did not allow Himself
to destroy them as their guilt deserved. Jerome says it means "in the breach of his wrath," which we say
as "in the breach of his wrath." The intercession is this: "If you forgive them their sin, forgive; but if not, blot me out of your book."
He was sure that God's justice would not want to blot him out, so he stood and offered himself for the guilty.
So their destruction was left undone. And they counted the desirable land as nothing. And the delightful land, the land of promise,
that is, the kingdom of heaven, they counted as nothing. They did not believe his word. Nor did they trust his promise.
And they murmured in their tents. And so they whispered in their lodgings, speaking reproaches against God and Moses.
They did not heed the voice of the Lord. And they did not heed the voice of God, which forbade them to murmur. And he lifted up his hand over them
to cast them down in the wilderness, and to cast down their seed among the nations, and to scatter them among the lands. Then he raised his hand over them
to fell them there in the wilderness, so that those of them who were left would be brought low among the peoples, and to scatter them through the countries. And they were ini-
-tiated into Baal-Peor. Initiated [?]: that is, they were consecrated to Priapus. As the apostle says, having come into a reprobate mind,
they raged so far that God's justice was openly shown upon them. And they ate the sacrifices of the dead.
And they ate the offerings of dead men, such as Priapus was. It is as if God spared them in these words, though they did even worse than that.
And they provoked him with their inventions. And with their devisings they angered him. They devised various gods.
And ruin was multiplied among them. And so their fall became manifold; they all lay dead in the wilderness.
And Phinehas stood and appeased him, and the shaking ceased. And Phinehas stood against the wrongdoing; by this he appeased God,
and so at that time the affliction was stilled. Here "quassatio" (shaking) is what was called "confractio" (breach) earlier, that is, their destruction.
And it was counted to him as righteousness, from generation to generation for ever. And that was counted to him as righteousness
in all generations; so it will be for ever. And they provoked him at the water of contradiction, and Moses was troubled because of them.
who embittered his spirit. Then they angered him again at the place that is called the water of contradiction,
because there they spoke against God. And there Moses was troubled because of those who made his mind bitter.
And he made a distinction with his lips. That is, in his words he set apart the wonder of God that they then demanded from the earlier wonders.
He trusted the earlier ones; this one he did not trust. Therefore, before he struck the rock with the rod, he said in doubt:
"CAN WE BRING WATER OUT OF THIS ROCK?" Through that doubt he too became guilty, and the guilt did not let him come
into the land of promise. But those who did come there, what did they do? They did not destroy the nations that the Lord had told them about.
They did not wipe out the peoples whom God had commanded them to wipe out: the Canaanites, Amorites, Jebusites and others. And they were mingled among the nations and learned their works,
and served their graven images, and it became a stumbling block to them. They mixed with them and married their daughters,
and acted as they did, and served their idols. That turned out badly for them. Scandalum is a Greek word
and means offense, or the left-hand side, since this mingling led them to the left side. And they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons,
and they shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed to the graven images of Canaan.
And from there they went so far astray that they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons. That was sacrilege.
And they shed the innocent blood of the very children they sacrificed to idols. That was both homicide and parricide at once.
They learned that from the nations. And the land was slain with blood, and was defiled by their works, and they committed fornication in their own inventions.
Through such innocent blood the earth was slain: not the earth itself, but those who dwelt on it
were slain on it. And it was defiled by their works, and so they played the harlot,
that is, in this way they betrayed God in their inventions. Were these inventions really their own? No. They belonged to the nations.
For this reason other translators said: in their pursuits, or in their affections, or in their affectations, or in their pleasures, or in their observances.
And the Lord was angry with fury against his people, and he abhorred his inheritance. Then God was angered by all this, against his people, and
loathed his inheritance, which they were supposed to be. And he handed them over into the hands of the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
And so he gave them into the hands of other peoples, and their enemies ruled over them. These were the Moabites, Ammonites, Philistines and Syrians.
And their enemies afflicted them, and they were humbled under their hands. And those enemies of theirs oppressed them, and under their hands they were brought low.
Because they would not be redeemed by the gracious God, they had to serve ungracious lords again. Many times he set them free.
However all that may have been, he still set them free many times, as is written in the Book of Judges.
But they embittered him with their counsel, and they were humbled in their iniquities. But they started again and failed him in their counsel.
their soul fainted within them. They grew weak from want, because they did not have what they longed for.
They wanted to know the way of truth. That is what they longed for. In this the philosophers could not help them.
What then? They cried to the Lord when they were in trouble, and he delivered them from their distresses. They cried out to God
when they were in such need, and he took them out of that need. The compunction came to them from him.
And he led them onto the right way, so that they might go to a city of habitation. And he led them onto the right way, to Christ,
so that in him they might go to the city of eternal dwelling. Let them confess to the Lord his mercies, and his wonders to the children of men,
for he has satisfied the empty soul and filled the hungry soul with good things. Therefore confess his mercy to the Lord, you,
and confess his wonders, you, to the children of men: that he filled the empty and hungry soul with good things.
How is this meant: "confess mercy and wonders"? Only that he bids those to confess who have experienced them.
Those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, and bound in beggary and iron. For he filled the Gentiles, who once sat in darkness
and in the shadow of death, and were bound with sins; in beggary, because they were poor; in iron, that is, in the hardness of evils.
That was one temptation. For they provoked the words of God and scorned the counsel of the Most High; and their heart was humbled in labours; they were weakened,
and there was no one to help them. For they too, having come to the knowledge of the truth, spoke against God's word and his will,
not submitting to the righteousness of God and wishing to establish their own. And therefore their heart was humbled in the struggles
that they had undertaken in vain against the desires. Then they gave way under necessity, because there was no one to help them,
since God did not help them. But what then? They cried to the Lord when they were in trouble, and he freed them from their distresses.
And he led them out of darkness and the shadow of death and broke their bonds asunder. Then he took them a second time out of darkness and out of death
and out of bonds. Let them confess to the Lord his mercies, and his wonders to the children of men. For he has shattered the gates of bronze
and broken the bars of iron. Now let there again be confession of this: that he broke the bronze gates and the iron bars.
He took them up from the way of their iniquity; for because of their injustices they were humbled. And he took them away from the way of unrighteousness,
in that they wanted to be good without him; but they were first humbled because of those same unrighteous deeds.
That was the second temptation: the first was of ignorance, this one was of presumption. Their soul loathed all food,
and they drew near even to the gates of death. They loathed all food, because disgust for spiritual goods came upon them.
That also brought them to the gates of hell. But what then? They cried to the Lord when they were in trouble, and he freed them from their distresses.
He sent his word and healed them. For that too was an evil wound, and they were sick with that sickness.
Where, then, is their good? Evils have come to them in place of good things. He turned the desert into pools of water, and land without water into springs of water.
In contrast, he made the wilderness into standing waters, and waterless earth into running waters.
And he settled the hungry there. And there, by the waters, he placed the hungry. And they founded a city to live in. And they built a city and lived there.
And they sowed fields and planted vineyards, and produced the fruit of birth. And they worked for grain and wine, and had children. And he bl-
-essed them, and they multiplied greatly. And he made them prosper and grow, and so many of them came from a few.
And their cattle did not decrease. And their livestock lasted. Who does not know that all this was said about the Gentiles?
They were scorched [?]. So they were barren and bore no fruit of good works, and they were hungry and thirsty for the holy faith.
He remedied this for them, because plentiful teaching came to them from him. They lived by it, and so did their beasts of burden,
that is, those who live simply in the church, because he ordered that all of them be taught, both the quick and the slow. And they became few and were afflicted
by the trouble of evils and by sorrow. The same people became few through those who separated from them. These were the same in appearance but not in truth.
And they were afflicted by the torment of woes and by grief. This rightly happened to heretics and schismatics,
whom division made few, because they were not united. Contempt is poured out on princes. On the princes of religion, as it seemed to them,
contempt was cast, because holy church paid no heed to them. And he made them wander where there is no road
and not on the way. And God made them stray where there is no road, not on the way. He let them go in the desires of their heart,
because they led themselves astray, THINKING THEMSELVES TO BE SOMETHING WHEN THEY ARE NOTHING. And he helped the poor man out of want.
In contrast, he helped the poor man out of poverty. For whoever is humble and recognizes that he is poor,
him he helps. And he made families like sheep. And he set the family of such people like sheep, because he did not leave them without a shepherd.
The upright will see and rejoice. The righteous see this and rejoice at it; they rejoice in each other's company.
And all wickedness shut its mouth. And all injustice closed its mouth, because it found no objection to make.
Who is wise? And he will keep these things, and he understands the mercies of the Lord. Who is now as wise as this requires?
Whoever is wise, let him keep these things in his mind, and he will recognize God's grace.
A SONG OF A PSALM FOR DAVID HIMSELF. MY HEART IS READY, O GOD, MY HEART IS READY. The Son speaks to the Father:
My heart is ready; ready is my heart. Ready for what? For enduring the Passion. I will sing and play psalms in my glory.
To you I sing; to you I sing psalms in my glory. Arise, my glory; arise, psaltery and harp.
Arise, my glory; show yourself by rising again and by ascending. Arise, psaltery and harp: these are the miracles and the sufferings.
May they deprive him of every good thing. Let there be no one to help him, nor anyone to have mercy on his orphans. And to his orphans
