let no one give help or mercy. Let his children be brought to destruction; in one generation let his name be blotted out. Let his children be lost;
let his own name pass away in one generation; let him not attain a second generation. Let the iniquity of his fathers come back into remembrance in the sight of the Lord,
and let the sin of his mother not be blotted out. Let the injustice of his forefathers be remembered before God, and let his mother's sins not be wiped out.
Let him who came as evil from the evil be lost together with them. As it is written:
I WILL REPAY THE SINS OF THE FATHERS UPON THE SONS WHO HATE ME. If he had been willing to be good, their sins would not have harmed him. Let them always be against the Lord,
so that their memory may perish from the earth. Let the forefathers be against God; let their sins be before him, for other translators said "before God" (coram deo),
so that their memory may pass away from the land of the living. Because he did not remember to show mercy, and persecuted the poor and needy man,
and put to death the one who was pierced in heart. Because he showed no mercy to Christ, and slew him, who was poor, begging, and sorrowful.
The second and the third refer more to his members. If, following other versions, it is to read "mortificare" (to put to death), then it is
"ut mortificaret" (in order to put to death). And he loved cursing, and it shall come to him; he did not want blessing, and it shall be far from him. He loved cursing, both he and the people;
it comes upon him: Judas by stealing, selling, and betraying; the people by saying: HIS BLOOD BE ON US AND ON OUR CHILDREN.
He did not want blessing; it goes far from him. Judas did not want Christ, who is the blessing. The people did not want the blessing
when the one who had been enlightened by the Lord said to them: DO YOU ALSO WANT TO BECOME HIS DISCIPLES?
and they said, as a curse: YOU BE HIS DISCIPLE. And for that reason the blessing went from them to the gentiles.
And he put on cursing like a garment, and it entered like water into his inward parts. And like a garment he put on the curse,
whether Judas or the people; and like water it came into him. Body and soul earned hell: the body outwardly, the soul inwardly.
And like oil into his bones. And like oil it came into his bones, because doing evil was pleasing to him,
as oil is pleasant for a man to swallow. Let it be to him like the garment with which he is covered, and like the girdle with which he is always girded.
Since it pleases him, let it be to him like the garment that covers him. As that shows on him,
so let the curse show on him. And as the belt with which he always girds himself makes him ready for work,
so let the curse make him ready for doing evil. According to these words, we always see the Jews prone to evil.
This is the work of those who disparage me before the Lord, and who speak evil against my soul. This is the work of heretics, as well as of Jews,
who belittle me before God and deny me equality with the Father, and who speak evil against me. And you,
Lord, Lord, deal with me for your name's sake. And you, Lord, my Father, work together with me; help me in my work.
...who wanted to gain riches by selling Christ. Here, however, the Lord is at the right hand of the poor man, so that the Lord himself may be his riches.
And that his soul may be kept safe from the persecutors. He also promised this to the martyrs, who would not consent to the persecutors
in evil, because God was at their right hand.
A Psalm of David. The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand. David the prophet speaks here: To my lord Christ
my Lord, his Father, said: Sit at my right hand. Where did David hear this? In the spirit. In whose spirit?
God's. He learned it through his inward teaching. The Spirit knows all the secrets of God. The voices of all the prophets are his.
Christ is David's lord according to his divinity; he is also David's son according to the flesh. Yet there are not two lords in the Father and the Son,
even though it says "the Lord to the Lord", but one God. In human affairs, too, a private man can have a son who is king as his lord,
and a son who has been made a bishop can be called the father of his father. But since the Father and the Son are one, how then did the Father command the Son like this:
"Sit at my right hand"? Only on account of the humanity he took on, in which the Son is less than the Father. What did he say?
Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet, that is, put them under your feet. Sit beside me
until I put your enemies under your feet. Are not all the nations that were once his enemies now subject to him? As it says elsewhere:
I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession. Whether willingly or unwillingly, all of them are under his feet.
Blessed are those who are there willingly; wretched are those who are there unwillingly. The Lord will send forth the rod of your power out of Zion. Out of Zion God sends forth the rod of your power.
As it says: Out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. The kingdom of your power begins at Jerusalem; from there it goes out to the ends
of the earth. Rule in the midst of your enemies. Be mighty in the midst of your enemies: in the midst of pagans,
Jews, heretics, and false brethren. With you is the beginning in the day of your power. Who is speaking now? The Father to the Son.
What does he say? I am together with you. I am what you are. I am the Beginning, and so are you. We are undivided.
Therefore there are not two beginnings, but one beginning. In the beginning was the Word. It always was, and still is. What does this mean?
The Word, the Beginning, is in the Father, the Beginning. In the day of your power: this shines forth on the day of your power. To whom? To all the saints,
because, having now been made like you, they will see you as you are. You give that power, and there you have it.
It is lost to the impious, because they do not see the glory of God. In the splendours of the saints. When the splendour of the saints comes, which consists in this:

that they become conformed to the image of God, then "with you is the beginning" shines forth. From the womb, before the morning star, I begot you. Before the stars, before time, out of the hidden depths of my substance
I begot you. But how was it in time? Was that not also before the morning star? For the Lord was born at night from the womb of the Virgin Mary.
Who knows this? The shepherds keeping the night watches over their flock, sent by the angel to see this word.
ALLELUIA OF THE RETURN OF HAGGAI AND ZECHARIAH. These two prophets turned their minds to the spiritual meaning
when, after returning from Babylon, they saw the renewal of the temple, because it signifies the restoration of the new people, which is in Christ.
Therefore this psalm is the alleluia of that holy return, which David sang in his own time, fourteen generations before.
BLESSED IS THE MAN WHO FEARS THE LORD. Blessed is the man who fears God. He will delight greatly in his commandments.
And he is very eager in his commandments, so that he gladly carries them out. His seed will be mighty on earth.
His seed, that is, good work, has great power in the land of the blessed. That land was granted to Zacchaeus
for half of his goods, and to the widow for two mites, and to the poor man for a cup of cold water. That is how mighty the seed of good works is.
The generation of the upright shall be blessed. The offspring of the righteous will be called blessed. What is their seed is their generation, and
blessedness follows it, that is, a blessing. Old people gave a blessing to their children, and that was called benedicere ["to bless"].
Glory and riches are in his house. Glory and wealth are in the heart of the one who fears the Lord. In it is the hope of eternal life;
in it he has enough, because his hope will be turned into reality. And his righteousness endures for ever and ever.
Therefore he is rich, because his righteousness lasts forever. He did it in time; he has it in eternity. Where has this come from?
A light has risen in the darkness for the upright in heart: the Lord is merciful, compassionate and just. For a light has risen in the darkness for the upright in heart.
What is that light? The Lord, who is just toward the wicked and merciful toward the good. Why only the upright in heart? Because it is written:
HE CAME TO HIS OWN, AND HIS OWN DID NOT RECEIVE HIM. BUT TO ALL WHO RECEIVED HIM, HE GAVE POWER TO BECOME SONS OF GOD.
Pleasant is the man who shows mercy and lends. Delightful is the person who shows mercy to another and lends. Or it means one who pardons another and forgives him
and gives. This agrees with what is written: FORGIVE, AND YOU WILL BE FORGIVEN. GIVE, AND IT WILL BE GIVEN TO YOU. For each one of them is merciful
who gives to another, or forgives, or lends. Whoever wants to take revenge for himself is seeking glory. But because it is written,
HE WHO CONQUERS ANGER IS BETTER THAN HE WHO STORMS A CITY, the one who becomes the better victor by pardoning is not without glory.
In the same way, whoever will not give to the poor is seeking riches. But he does not become poor by giving, because the heavenly treasure is the most secure.
He will order his words in judgment. He sets his words in order on the Day of Judgment, where the whole sworn verdict [literally "oath-staff"]
will depend on works of mercy. He finds this good order for them: LORD, YOU HANDED OVER FIVE TALENTS TO ME;
SEE, I HAVE GAINED FIVE MORE. He will be defended by these, as is shown there. For he shall not be moved for ever.
For he will never again be separated from God's right hand. The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance.
The righteous man remains in eternal remembrance. This remembrance is denied to the wicked in the words, I DO NOT KNOW YOU. He shall not be afraid of evil news.
He does not fear what the wicked are to hear: "Go into the eternal fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels."
His heart is ready to hope in the Lord. It is for this reason: that his heart is ready to hope in God, and in him to overcome all temptations.
His heart is strengthened. His heart is made firm against those who insult him on that account, because he hopes for what he does not see.
He shall not be moved until he looks down upon his enemies. He is so firmly established that he does not fall away from that hope before he sees, from above,
what his enemies will see from below: they on earth, and he in heaven. He has scattered abroad, he has given to the poor.
For that reason he distributed his goods and gave them to the poor. His righteousness endures for ever and ever. That is, his righteousness lasts forever,
because he who wished to hunger and thirst on earth in the poor has kept it for him in heaven. His horn shall be exalted in glory.
His horn will be gloriously exalted, because he will be mighty before God. The sinner shall see it and be angry.
The sinner sees this and is angry with himself in a penitence that comes too late. He shall gnash with his teeth and waste away.
He gnashes with his teeth and wastes away, because he has been cast to the place where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth. To him
it is not granted to flourish and grow green again, as would have happened if he had done penance at the proper time.
Why so? The desire of sinners shall perish. He has put it off until the place where the craving of sinners comes to nothing.
Alleluia. Praise the Lord, you children; praise the name of the Lord. Praise the Lord, children; praise the Lord's name.
Let everyone be a child, be humble, and praise God, not himself. If he is willing to be a child,
then he can pass through the narrow way, then he can come to heaven, for narrow is the gate that leads there.
Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and for evermore. Praised be the Lord's name from now into eternity,
that is to say, both now and forever. From the rising of the sun to its going down the name of the Lord is to be praised. To all who dwell from the rising to the setting,
as far as holy Church reaches, let his name be worthy of praise. The Lord is high above all nations.
The Lord is high above all peoples. Peoples are human beings; who does not know that he is higher than they are?
His glory is above the heavens. His glory is also above the heavens. His heavens are the humble, in whom he dwells,
who know him to be above them. Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high and looks upon lowly things? Who is like our God, who sits on high
and looks upon lowly things? He who sits upon the high heavens, why should he not see the lowly things on earth? But it says:
and looks upon lowly things in heaven and on earth. In his saints, who, though placed in the flesh, live their lives in heaven, he has heaven and earth.
Since they are both heaven and earth, and are humble, he therefore looks upon lowly things in heaven and on earth.
They are heaven, because they set their minds on the things that are above; they are earth, because they are not yet released from the fle-
…is also in hope of what he does not yet have in reality. Therefore he is also their helper and protector. Those who fear the Lord have hoped in the Lord.
He is their helper and their protector. Those who fear God hope in him. Therefore he is their helper and protector.
The Lord has been mindful of us and has blessed us. By his grace, without our merit, our God remembered us and gave us blessing.
He has blessed the house of Israel; he has blessed the house of Aaron; he has blessed all who fear the Lord, the small together with the greater. Both to the hoping and
to the fearing, the greater and the lesser, he gave his blessing. May the Lord add more upon you, upon you and upon your children.
May the Lord add still more to you, to you and to your children. May the Lord make you grow,
you teachers of the house of Aaron and you hearers of the house of Israel, until holy Church is spread throughout the whole world.
Blessed are you by the Lord, who made heaven and earth, that is, who made us. You are named for good by the Lord,
who made some of you heaven, from which the rain comes, and others earth, which is rained upon.
The heaven of heaven is the Lord's, but the earth he has given to the children of men. The teachers of the teachers he kept for himself to teach,
because they could not be taught by anyone else. The carnal, who are called earth, he gave to be taught by the children of men who had already become heaven,
so that the lower might be watered by the higher. The dead shall not praise you, O Lord, nor any who go down into hell.
Heaven and earth praise you. The dead do not praise you, nor do those who go to hell. Who are they? Who but those who want to live from themselves?
But we who live bless the Lord, from this time now and forever. But we, living by God's grace, give thanks to him forever.
ALLELUIA. I HAVE LOVED, BECAUSE THE LORD WILL HEAR THE VOICE of my prayer. I loved God, because he heard the voice of my prayer.
Because he has inclined his ear to me. Because he held his ear to me. How does a person know that, except from hope?
And in my days I will call upon him. And in my days I call upon him. Those are the days of my misery,
the days of my mortality, which came upon me through disobedience. The sorrows of death have surrounded me; the perils of hell
have found me. In those days the pains of death surrounded me; the perils of hell found me out.
Where did they find me out? Where did they find me? Wandering away from you. They found me; I could not find them.
I could not recognize them. In the prosperity of the world: that is where the perils of hell mostly lie. I was caught in them, and they did not let me know them.
Therefore I lamented them to you. I found tribulation and sorrow, and I will call upon the name of the Lord. But I came to myself and reflected,
and found in myself the hardships and pains that had lain on me without my knowing it, and I called upon God's name, because then I knew who I was.
O Lord, deliver my soul. Ah, Lord, I said, set my soul free. Every person needs this:
to hurry to find the misery that lies on him without his knowing it, and to say: I HAVE FOUND TRIBULATION AND SORROW.
[?] me, God. His is the help; in him I hope. All nations surrounded me, and in the name of the Lord I took vengeance on them, that is, on the peoples of the Gentiles.
Me, your people, says the Church, all nations surrounded, and in your name I overcame them.
Surrounding they surrounded me, and in the name of the Lord I took vengeance on them. Me myself, says Christ, the Jews surrounded, and I overcame them in your name.
They surrounded me like bees a honeycomb. As bees surround the honeycombs, they surrounded me, for with the Passion they made me sweeter
to all who loved the mystery. And they blazed up like fire among thorns. And in my body they burned like fire in thorns,
for they burned away the pricks of the flesh with the fire of persecution. The Gentiles did that. And in the name of the Lord I took vengeance on them.
And in God's name I avenged it on them, either through the conversion of penance or through future vengeance.
Pushed, I was overturned so that I might fall. Being pushed, I was turned so that I would fall. What one wants to remove,
if it stands firm, one shakes it, one turns it about. So the persecutors did to me; so they wanted to fell me.
Or: being pushed, I was turned as one turns bread on the hearth, that is, I was turned over again and again,
so that, pushed often, I would fall. But the Lord upheld me. But God caught me, so that I did not fall. Another edition says:
LIKE A HEAP OF SAND I WAS PUSHED SO THAT I MIGHT FALL. Like the heap of sand I was pushed so that I would fall.
What falls more easily? But God did not let me fall. The Lord is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation.
My strength and my praise is the Lord, and he has become salvation for me. He falls from a push
who wants to be his own strength and his own praise. But because God does not fall, therefore he does not fall who holds fast to him.
The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous. There is the voice of joy and salvation where the dwellings of the righteous are, not the voice of sorrow,
as their enemies supposed. The right hand of the Lord has done mighty deeds; the right hand of the Lord has exalted me. God's right hand worked strength in me.
God's right hand raised me up. His power is to exalt the humble, to make the mortal divine, to grant glory out of subjection,
victory out of suffering. I shall not die, but live, and tell the works of the Lord. Therefore I, his Church, shall not die,
but I shall live and tell his works. Why did he want me to suffer such things? The Lord chastening has chastened me,
and he has not handed me over to death. Correcting, he corrected me; he did not let me die. To what end did he correct me?
Only so that I might possess the inheritance, as a father whips the son whom he intends for the inheritance. Where is the inheritance?
Open to me the gates of righteousness; having entered them, I will give praise to the Lord. Open to me. Which ones? You apostles, who received the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
Open to me the gates of the kingdom of God, to which righteousness leads; there I will find it. Having gone in there, I will give praise to God in songs of praise,
as it says: BLESSED ARE THEY WHO DWELL IN YOUR HOUSE; FOR EVER AND EVER THEY WILL PRAISE YOU. These are the gates of the Lord.
These gates are the Lord's. For whom [are they], within? Which ones go in there? The righteous shall enter into it.
The righteous go in there. I will confess to you, Lord, for you have heard me, and you have become my salvation.
There I confess to you, Lord; there I thank you that you heard me and have become salvation for me.
The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner. The stone that the Jews rejected as they built became the head of the
corner, that is, the headstone. The headstone is the cornerstone, which joins both walls together.
Christ joined together the uncircumcised and the circumcised, so that in him they would be one people, one Church. This was done by the Lord.
It came about from God. By the Jews he was built up according to the flesh; by God he became the cornerstone,
not by the Jews who were building, for they rejected him because of the flesh. And it is wonderful in our eyes. And in our eyes it is wonderful.
In the eyes of the inner man, in the eyes of those who believe, hope, and love. This is the day which the Lord has made. That is the day which God made,
the day of our salvation, on which God made him the head of the corner. Let us exult and rejoice in it. On it let us rejoice,
on that day let us be glad and joyful. O Lord, save me; O Lord, give good success. Yes, you, Lord, keep me safe.
Lord, make my journey to you go well, for I am returning from far exile and parting from those
who hated peace, with whom I spoke peaceably, and yet they fought against me without cause. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
Blessed is he who comes in the Lord's name; cursed is he who comes in his own name. As it says in the Gospel:
I have come in my Father's name, and you did not receive me. If another comes in his own name, him you will receive.
We have blessed you from the house of the Lord. We blessed you out of God's house. Who say this?
The priests to the people, the great to the little ones; so great that in their minds they reach to the Word, God with God,
as far as that can be in this life; and yet they temper their speech for the sake of the little ones, so that they can say with the apostle: For whether we are beside ourselves,
it is for God; or whether we are restrained, it is for you. Where do they get this? Where does it come to them from? Only from heaven,
where the inner house of God is. What do they proclaim? God is the Lord, and he has shone upon us. The Lord who has come in the name of the Lord, whom the Jews rejected as they built,
he is God, equal to the Father. And he has shone upon us. He made this manifest to us, so that we too may make it clear to you,
and that you may understand it together with us, that you may believe together with us. Appoint a festal day with crowded throngs, even to the horn of the altar.
Set yourselves a festal day, and keep it in the throng; gather a multitude to it; set it for yourselves here in the throng,
where the Lamb was slain, until you come up there to the inner house of God, from where we gave you the blessing,
where the horns of the altar are high. There is the voice of exultation, the sound of one celebrating a festival, of those walking in the place of the tabernacle.
Did Paul, then, not walk in His ways, Paul who confesses sin, which is iniquity? What does he say?
FOR WHAT I DO NOT WANT, THAT I DO. NOW IT IS NO LONGER I WHO DO IT, BUT THE SIN THAT DWELLS IN ME.
The works of sin were not his works, because the sin that was in him worked them against his will.
Every person has desire in him. If he follows it, he cannot say with Paul: NOW IT IS NO LONGER I WHO DO IT. But if he does not follow it,
then he does and does not do, as Paul's own words put it, for he said: I DO AND I DO NOT DO. His weakness acts and struggles;
his will does not act, because it struggles against it. From this you should know that those who consent to evil do not walk in the ways of the Lord.
The same apostle forbade such consent, saying: THEREFORE LET NOT SIN REIGN IN YOUR MORTAL BODY
SO THAT YOU OBEY ITS DESIRES. You have commanded that your commandments be kept exceedingly. You commanded that your commandments be kept diligently,
that they be carried out diligently. Here "nimis" stands for "valde" ("very"). It has two senses. One, among the Greeks, is "agan",
which means "too much". The other is "spodra", which means "much", "greatly" and "diligently". O that my ways may be directed to keep your justifications.
Since you commanded that they be carried out diligently, I wish that my ways may be turned rightly toward keeping them.
What are justifications but commandments that make people just? What are they, says Saint Augustine, but deeds of righteousness,
the works of the just that God commands? And why are they called his, except that he directs [?] them? So we may render them as "frumereht" ("rules of good deeds")
or "werchreht" ("rules of works"). Then I shall not be put to shame when I look into all your commandments. Then I shall not be ashamed
when I look into all your commandments. The ones I did not carry out bring me shame. I will confess to you in uprightness of heart,
in that I have learned the judgments of your justice. So I will praise you in the uprightness of my heart for having learned your just judgments,
if my ways are directed by you. Then the praise is yours, not mine. If my heart is directed and my ways are directed, I shall rejoice in them;
I shall not be accused in them. I will keep your justifications. Understood again: if my ways are directed. Then I will keep your rules of good deeds;
otherwise I cannot. Do not forsake me utterly. Never forsake me. Or it means "usque valde" ("very greatly"), with this sense:
However much you forsook me when you did not guard me, do not forsake me so completely that I become lost.
If you forsook me so that I would not glory in myself, do not do it utterly; and once I am justified by you, I will glory in you. WHEREWITH DOES A YOUNGER MAN CORRECT HIS WAY?
By what does the young man set his way straight? This question is answered thus: By keeping your words. By keep-
-ing your words, that is, by carrying them out. Why the young man rather than the old, unless it is that he should begin this while young
and complete it when older? Let us also see who represents the old man and who the new: the former does not keep God's words; the latter keeps them.
So this one is the young man of whom it is said: With my whole heart I have sought you. With all my heart.
There you did not want to be. Where are you, then, now, except in misery? Is that not spoken as a rebuke?
And has this rebuke not become our inheritance in our manifold tribulations? Which are, for that reason, so heavy and so manifold.
For they did evil not through weakness or ignorance, but through pride. Cursed are those who turn aside from your commandments. Named for evil are those whom this does not frighten,
and who, even beyond that, still turn away from your commandments. Take away from me reproach and contempt, for your testimonies
that is, your martyrdoms, I have sought out. Take away from me, says Holy Church, reproach and contempt, for I have sought your testimonies.
Now that has come to pass. Now there is no reproach or contempt for anyone in confessing Christ and standing firm in his testimony,
for persecution has passed away. It has availed so well that she loved her enemies and prayed for them,
not fearing reproach and contempt, but caring for their salvation. For princes sat and spoke against me. The highest lords themselves sat
and talked against me, and held council about me. That is why the persecution was severe, for kings decreed that there should be no Christians anywhere.
But your servant was exercised in your justifications. But I, your servant, was exercised in your ordinances.
How was this exercise carried out? For your testimonies are my meditation. It was carried out in this way: your martyrdoms are my meditations.
I am so intent on them that I want to stand firm in them, and persecution cannot take them from me.
And your justifications are my counsel. And your ordinances are what I have resolved on, what I have committed myself to.
For I want to love my enemies and pray for them. In this I exercise myself; in these two things I strive to be unconquered,
so that by them I may be tempered and hardened for the sake of your name. My soul has cleaved to the pavement.
My soul clung to the floor; it followed the flesh, it stuck fast to earthly things. Because that is death,
quicken me. Therefore quicken me, and make me cleave to you, not to the flesh. He who just now said, 'But your servant
was exercised in your justifications,' now says, 'My soul has cleaved to the pavement.' Why, unless his exercise does not seem enough to him
and he wants to come further than the point he has reached? According to your word. Quicken me according to your promise,
which says to you: 'In Isaac shall your seed be called.' Make me a son of the promise, for it is not the sons of the flesh who are the sons of God,
but the sons of the promise. My ways, namely my evil ones, I have declared. My ways, that is, my sins, I told to you;
I confessed them to you. And you heard me. And you heard me in such a way that you forgave them to me. Teach me your justifications.
Teach me your ordinances; teach me to walk your ways. Teach me not only to know
but to do what I ought, for he knows the good who shows it. Instruct me in the way of your justifications, and I shall be exercised in your wonders,
that is, in your justifications. Teach me the way of your righteous works, and so I shall busy myself with your wonders that are in them.
and train me in them. Bring me to those things which I have not yet reached, which are so wonderful.
That is, [wonderful to] those who do not trust, who have not tasted them. My soul has slumbered for weariness. I slumbered for weariness,
because in hoping for those high things I grew faint, and I did not succeed in reaching them, however much I hoped for it.
Strengthen me in your words. Yet make me steadfast in those words of yours which I have attained,
so that I may go on from them to others. Remove the way of iniquity from me. Take the way of unrighteousness from me, for that is how it can best succeed.
And have mercy on me with your law. And be gracious to me with your law: with the law of faith, which by grace lets us do what
we could not do by ourselves, and not with the law of works, which came so that sin might abound. I have chosen the way of truth;
I have not forgotten your judgments. I have clung to your testimonies, Lord; do not put me to shame. I chose the way of truth, to walk on it.
I did not forget your judgments, so as to keep to the course. I clung to your testimonies until I walked in them.
My Lord, do not put me to shame by letting me fail to reach the place I aim for. For it does not depend on the one who wills, nor on the one who runs,
but on God who shows mercy. I have run the way of your commandments when you enlarged my heart. I ran the way of your commandments when you broadened my heart.
A heart full of desire is broad. That is what makes us say: "The love of God has been poured out in our hearts
through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us." That is why I could run, because you deigned to enlarge my heart.
Set a law for me, O Lord. Set a law for me, Lord. You set it for me in the letter; set it for me in the spirit. For the letter kills,
but the spirit gives life. You wrote it on tablets of stone; write it on the tablets of the heart. The way of your justifications:
set for me the way of your justifications as a law. Bring about righteousness in my heart through the law of faith, which makes a person willing.
For the unwilling person is not a friend of the law, even if he does the work of the law. Since he would gladly [?] have it uncommanded,
he is not made clean by the deed, because he is unclean in his will. And I will seek it always. And I will always seek that way.
How can that be? Did he not say, "I have run the way of your commandments"? Is that anything other than the way of God's justifications? No. How
then does he seek the way he is already on? Only in the sense that he wants to make progress on it, and to become so ready
that on it he may attain the prize of God's upward calling. Give me understanding, and I will search your law. Give me understanding,
and then I will search your law and learn in it the love of God and of neighbour. And I will keep it with my whole heart. And I will keep it in these two,
with all my heart. And I will also learn from it why you wanted to set it for those
who were not going to keep it, and how much use there is in it. For the law came in so that sin might abound.
Lead me in the path of your commandments, for I have desired it. Lead me on the path of your commandments, because I wanted it.
In your righteousness give me life. See now, I wanted your commandments; I longed for them. Give me life in your righteousness, not in mine.
What can kill me is in me. What I live by, I find nowhere but in you. Christ is your righteousness.
Redeem me in him. And let your mercy come upon me, Lord. And may your grace, Lord, come over me,
so that I may fulfil your commandments. What is this grace? Your salvation: Christ, your Savior,
who is your mercy and righteousness and truth. Let him become incarnate. In this way your mercy has come upon me,
according to your word, that is, according to your promise, as you promised Abraham. And I will give an answer, a word, to those who reproach me.
And so I will answer. With what? With the Word to those who reproach me: with Christ to those who reproach me, to whom it is a stumbling block or foolishness
that he was crucified. Or it means: I answer those who reproach me with the word of faith. What is that?
Nothing but what the Holy Spirit taught me, according to the promise: "For it is not you who speak,
but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you." As it says next: Because I have hoped in your words,
that is, in your promises. That is why I answered; that is why I was able to do it, because you
promised it. This is the voice of the body of Christ. And do not take away, that is, do not let be taken from my mouth, the word of truth utterly,
that is, in any way. And never take the word of truth from my mouth at all. For those also belong to the body of Christ
who could not endure persecution and denied Christ, and afterwards were nevertheless received back by the Church through their penance,
or were even brought to martyrdom a second time and won the palm. Therefore it is understood here that theirs is the voice that prays like this: Do not let me go as far as the deed,
nor deny you utterly. For although Peter denied him for an hour, he was nevertheless restored through weeping, and afterwards bravely crowned.
That is why the Savior said to him: "I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail." That is, that the word of truth may not be taken from your mouth
utterly. For I have hoped exceedingly in your judgments. Because I gained so much more hope in your judgments,
the more rebuke I suffered in them. Your judgments threw me down when I relied on myself, and raised me up again when I was penitent,
weeping, and relying on you. Through this I gained your grace more firmly, in that I lost my pride.
And I will keep your law always, forever and ever. And if you do not take the word of truth from my mouth,
then I will keep your law always. Which law? Love, which is the fulfilment of the law. I will keep your body,
your Church, forever and ever, for in the other world, where we see you, love will be fuller,
love of God and of neighbor. And I walked in a broad place. He who prayed earlier now tells what his prayer achieved.
It is as if he said: I prayed, you heard me, and so I walked in a broad place; I walked in chari- [?]
[?]…ty. Why is that? Because I have sought out your commandments. Because I sought your commandments, as you teach in the Gospel: "Seek, and you shall find."
And again: "Your Father from heaven will give the good Spirit to those who ask him." And I spoke of your testimonies in the sight of kings
and was not put to shame. And with that boldness I spoke, in your martyrs, before kings, and was not ashamed, as you promised in the Gospel:
"that we would confess you before kings." And I meditated on your commandments, which I loved. And I thought on your commandments. Which ones?
The love of God and of one's neighbour. And I lifted up my hands to your commandments, which I loved. And I raised up my hands to your commandments
which I loved. By the work I showed that I loved them; and I raised up my hands, because that to which I raised them
is on high. As it says: "I show you a more excellent way." And again:
"to know also the love of Christ, which surpasses knowledge." If anyone seeks the reward of earthly happiness for the work of God,
he lets his hands drop. And I was exercised in your justifications. And thereby I was exercised in your righteous works.
Other translators say "I rejoiced" or "I chattered" instead of "I was exercised," because he who loves God's justice practises it with gladness.
Remember your word to your servant, in which you have given me hope. Remember your word to your servant,
that is, your promise, in which you gave me hope. You have promised grace to the humble. They need it when temptation or
tribulation comes; therefore remember them. This has comforted me in my humiliation. That hope comforted me in my lowliness,
which has come to me from Adam, or in that which has come to me from persecutors. For your word has given me life. Because what you spoke,
that made me live; that comforted me unto life. What is that? Nothing but your promise that I, though cast down into death,
shall nevertheless rise again to life. The proud acted very unjustly. The proud did great wrong in this:
that they were impious, and forced us, the pious, to be impious together with them. They did great wrong, seeing that their pride
not even the humility of mortality has tamed. But I have not turned aside from your law. But I did not swerve from your law, as they wished.
I remembered your judgments from of old, O Lord, and was comforted. I remembered your judgments, which you have carried out from the beginning upon the vessels of wrath
that are destined for perdition; and that comforted me, because even through them you showed the riches of your glory toward the vessels of mercy.
How? In that you made them better by means of those. Weariness held me back from sinners who forsake your law.
Weariness came upon me because of sinners who forsake your law. I grew weary of living alongside
those among whom one must live here in this life, until the threshing floor is winnowed. Your justifications were songs to me
in the place of my pilgrimage. But your justifications were of such sweetness to me that I could sing them;
so comforting were they to me here in exile. I remembered your name in the night, O Lord, and kept your law.
I remembered your name in the night, Lord, and kept your law. The night is the miseries of mortality.
The night is the proud, who act unjustly beyond measure. The night is the weariness caused by sinners who forsake the law of God. The night is
the place of this pilgrimage, until the Lord comes and lights up the hidden things of darkness.
Here in this night everyone should remember the name of God, because no one can keep His law except in His name,
as it says: OUR HELP IS IN THE NAME OF THE LORD. This has happened to me because I sought out your justifications.
This night has become an improvement for me. Which night? The humility of this mortality. How? In that I learn from it not to be proud.
For it came from pride. But it improves me by this: that I eagerly sought your justifications. This is like:
IT IS GOOD FOR ME THAT YOU HAVE HUMBLED ME, SO THAT I MAY LEARN YOUR JUSTIFICATIONS. MY PORTION, LORD, I SAID, IS TO KEEP YOUR LAW.
My portion, Lord: I have said that I will keep your law, because no one else has a share in you except the one who keeps it.
I have entreated your face with my whole heart. That is why I prayed to your face with all my heart,
so that the life-giving Spirit may help me in this, lest the letter kill. And what did I say? Have mercy on me according to your word.
Have mercy on me according to your promise, so that I may be a son of the promise in the seed of Abraham. I thought on my ways and turned my feet to your testimonies.
I thought about my ways, which displeased me, and turned them to your testimonies, so that they might be more righteous there.
TURN AWAY MY EYES SO THAT THEY DO NOT SEE VANITY. Turn my eyes away so that they do not see vanity,
and likewise the feet, so that they do not go astray. This is like: MY EYES ARE EVER TOWARD THE LORD,
FOR HE WILL PLUCK MY FEET OUT OF THE SNARE. I am ready and am not troubled, so that I may keep your commandments. I am ready to keep
your commandment, and I am untroubled, because no fear takes it from me. The cords of sinners have wrapped around me, and I have not forgotten your law.
As is shown there: the rope of the sinners wrapped around me, and still I did not forget your law. The sinners are both the carnal
and the spiritual enemies. They lengthen their wickedness like a rope, because they keep tying one piece to another, and with it they wrap up the just,
by threatening evils and promising temporal goods. That rope was escaped by the one who speaks here: At midnight I rose to confess to you
because of the judgments of your justice. In the most bitter persecution I rose to confess to you, that is, to praise you,
for the judgments of your justice, because they are just judgments, that you will the just to be wrapped in the cord of sinners.
Why? Only so that they may be improved by it. I am a partaker with all who fear you and keep your commandments.
Now Christ speaks to the Father together with his body: I am a sharer with all who fear you and keep your commandments.
Christ says this because if he had not become a partaker in our mortality, we would not have become partakers in his divinity.
so that I, being so greatly compelled, may learn your justifications, and so that this may be the fruit of my humiliation. For he who does not heed the good,
that you humble him, and still does not mend his ways by it, things go worse for him. The law of your mouth is good to me
above thousands of gold and silver. Good to me is the law that comes from your mouth and is commanded by your mouth; it is better
than countless gold and silver. For my love (caritas) shall love the law of God more than greed (cupiditas) loves thousands of gold and silver.
YOUR HANDS, O LORD, HAVE MADE ME AND fashioned me; give me understanding, that I may learn your commandments. Your hands made me
and formed me; therefore give me understanding, so that I may learn your commandments. You gave me form; give me re-formation.
Since my nature was deformed by sinning, it has not been able to be whole in understanding. Therefore I am not fit to grasp the commandments of God unless I am renewed in the spirit of the mind.
Hands are named here to mean power, as also in the place where it says: AND HIS HANDS FOUNDED THE DRY LAND.
And again: THE HEAVENS ARE THE WORKS OF YOUR HANDS. And here Christ himself asks his Father for what he knows his body needs.
That need and that want he suffers in it, and he feels it, because its life is hidden with him in God.
Those who fear you shall see me and rejoice, because I have hoped beyond measure in your word. Those who fear you now shall see me at some time hereafter,
when the just shall shine like the sun; and then they will be glad. Who are they? None other than the people of holy Church, who now fear him.
They will then rejoice in their fear. This is because I hoped for more from your promise than I dared to ask.
As it says: GOD IS ABLE TO DO MORE THAN WE ASK OR UNDERSTAND. I have known, O Lord, that your judgments are equity,
and in your truth you have humbled me. I acknowledge, Lord, that your judgments are just, by which we have been cast into death,
and that in your truth you have humbled us. Let your mercy come to comfort me. After that let your grace come,
so that it may comfort me and I may be restored to life again. Let regeneration come to me; let faith, hope,
and love come to me, which here are the consolation of the wretched, not the joys of the blessed. According to your word to your servant.
According to your promise let it come to me, your servant. Let your mercies come to me, and I shall live. Let your mercies come to me, and then I shall live, and
live truly, so that I do not fear that I will die again. For your law is my meditation.
For your law is what I meditate on. My thought is in the faith that works through love; in that I do not fall short,
in that I live. Let the proud be confounded, because they have unjustly done wickedness against me; but I shall be exercised in your commandments. Let the proud be ashamed
that they acted unjustly against me; but I shall be exercised in your commandments, whatever they may do.
Let those who fear you turn to me, that is, toward me, and those who know your testimonies. These words cannot belong to anyone other than Christ.
"To me," says Christ, "let those be turned who fear you, Father, and who know your prophecies that were written about me."
I resolved to keep the judgments of your righteousness. These are they: that no one does evil with impunity
nor good in vain. I have been humbled exceedingly, Lord, that is, very greatly. Therefore I am greatly humbled in great persecution.
Give me life according to your word. Quicken me according to your promise, for the word of your promise is also a lamp to the feet and a light to the paths.
Make the freewill offerings of my mouth well-pleasing, Lord, that is, let them please you. May the willing offerings of my mouth be dear to you, which love (caritas) brings forth,
not fear. And teach me your judgments. And teach me your judgments. Earlier he said: I HAVE NOT TURNED ASIDE FROM YOUR JUDGMENTS.
How then does he now say, "Teach me your judgments"? Is it not that he wants to learn them better? My soul is always in my hands.
My soul is always in my hands. It is in my hands because I always bring it to you to be given life. As it says elsewhere:
TO YOU I HAVE LIFTED UP MY SOUL. Sinners have laid snares for me, and I have not strayed from your commandments. Sinners set snares for me,
and yet I was not led astray by them into turning away from your commandments, because I had brought my soul to you
for you to give it life. I have acquired your testimonies as an inheritance forever. As an inheritance I sought your testimonies forever.
That I may always confess you and never deny you: that I wish to have as my inheritance. Grant me that.
By your granting they can be an inheritance for me forever. For they are the rejoicing of my heart. For they are the joy of my heart,
even though they are an affliction to my body. I have inclined my heart to perform your justifications forever, for the sake of the reward.
I have inclined my heart to do your righteous deeds forever, for the reward. Justifications are works of love (caritas). Who can do them forever? When the needs
of our neighbours come to an end, the works also come to an end; but the rewards do not come to an end. Therefore he declares that he does justifications forever.
Earlier he said, praying: INCLINE MY HEART TO YOUR TESTIMONIES, to show that it is a divine gift.
But here he says I HAVE INCLINED, to show his own will as well. I HAVE HATED THE WICKED, AND I HAVE LOVED YOUR LAW.
I hated the unrighteous, and I loved your law. As much as I loved your law, so much I hated their unrighteousness.
I hated them in so far as they are wicked, not in so far as they are human beings. I did not hate human nature, but vice.
You are my helper and my protector. You are my helper to do good, my protector to escape evil.
I have hoped exceedingly in your word. I have hoped beyond measure in your promise, like a son of the promise. Depart from me, you wicked ones,
and I will search out the commandments of my God. Get away from me, you ill-willed ones, and then I will search out my God's commandments. Let me consider
what is dear to God, so that I may be bound to what comes first, not, as you wish, to what comes last.
These words are directed against those who importunately demand our help in worldly business. Uphold me according to your word, and I shall live,
and do not put me to shame in my expectation. Receive me according to your promise, and so I shall live. Where? Surely in the future.
...a little one, great things. And thirsting, I drank in the good Spirit, who helped me to do what I could not do through the commandment, holy

and just and good. For it is not those who are led by their own spirit, but those who are led by the Spirit of God, who are the sons of God. This is not because they themselves do nothing, but so that they do not fail to do good:
they are moved by the Good so that they may act. "Look upon me and have mercy on me, according to the judgment of those who love your name." Look upon me
and have mercy on me according to the judgment of those who love your name. That means: according to the judgment that you made on those
who love your name. Why do they love? Only because you loved them first. As John says: "Let us love God,
because he first loved us." These are the words of one who has drunk sweetness and, having tasted the sweetness,
wants to drink more. "Direct my steps according to your word, and let no iniquity have dominion over me." Direct
my steps according to your commandment, and let no injustice rule over me. You commanded love: give me love.
Since you were willing to command it, be willing also to help me toward it. "Redeem me from the false accusations of men, and I will keep your commandments."
Free me from the slanders of men, and then I will keep your commandment. Calumnies are false accusations. Make me not fear them.
Then I will be kept safe in their midst through patience. Whoever fears them is easily turned to follow them. Do not let that happen to me.
"Make your face shine upon your servant." Let your face shine over your servant. Show me your presence by helping me.
"And teach me your statutes." And teach me your statutes. Teach them to me in such a way that I do them.
So it also says elsewhere: "Teach me to do your will." For whoever does not do them has not learned them.
So says the Truth: "Everyone who has heard from the Father and has learned comes to me." From this it is true that whoever does not do,
therefore does not come, because he has not learned. "My eyes have brought down streams of water, because they did not keep your law."
My eyes brought down outflowings of water, because they did not keep your commandments.
My eyes, which carelessly looked on misdeeds, weep for it. Their stream had to flow downward, to the humility of penitence,
because of the guilt of having gazed at the allurements of unlawful curiosity. So it happened to David on account of Uriah's wife.
In other books it reads: "My eyes have passed over [streams of water]," as if eyes could run more than springs of water.
This figure of speech is called hyperbole, that is, overstepping. "You are just, O Lord, and your judgment is right."
You are just, Lord, and your judgment is right. Therefore I wept much,
because every sinner must fear your justice, by which you condemn whoever is condemned, and there is no one who can rightly complain about his condemnation.
"You have commanded justice, your testimonies." You commanded what is right. What? Your testimonies. They are your justice, and you are just
in commanding justice. "And your truth exceedingly." And you commanded your truth strictly. What truth? Again, those same testimonies.
by which you wish to make yourself known; these one must keep all the more diligently, the more diligently they are commanded.
My zeal has made me waste away, because my enemies have forgotten your words. My zeal made me waste away,
because my enemies forgot your words. Because I loved them, I was grieved that they were not, together with me, fervent in the love of God.
That grief weighed on me so heavily that it made me waste away as if in sickness. Hence it is written elsewhere:
The zeal for your house has consumed me. Your word is exceedingly fiery, and your servant has loved it. Your word glows and kindles fiercely,
and your servant loved it. That is why I also wanted my enemies to love it, and for it to set them on fire. Cleopas felt this
when he said: "Was not our heart burning within us while he opened the Scriptures to us on the way?" I am young and despised;
I have not forgotten your statutes. I am younger than they are, and despised; yet I did not forget your statutes,
as they did. The people of the New Testament may say this, who were held in contempt by the people of the Old Testament. This may also be said in particular by
Joseph and David, who were held in contempt by their brothers and yet kept the statutes of God. Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness.
Your righteousness is eternal righteousness, not that of the Jews, for their righteousness, which they wanted to set above the righteousness of God, is made void.
And your law is truth. And your law is truth, as is evident from the fact that it bears witness to the righteousness of God. As it says:
"The righteousness of God has been made manifest, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets." Trouble and anguish have found me; your commandments are my meditation.
What then has happened to me? Troubles and anxieties came upon me; yet your commandments were my thought.
Let them attack, let them help one another, let them persecute me; I only keep your commandments, and I even love them [my enemies] for the sake of your commandment.
Your testimonies are righteousness forever. Your testimonies, for which the martyrs died, are eternal righteousness, for they live forever by that righteousness.
Give me understanding, and I shall live. And give me understanding, and then I shall live. Make me understand how there is nothing
that persecuting enemies can take from me, and how I will then truly live if I lose temporal life
for the sake of confessing you. I have cried out with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord; I will seek your statutes.
I called with all my heart. This is what someone does who is intent on his prayer and in his earnestness does not let himself think of anything else.
Such prayer is constant for some, not for many. Whether it is ever so perfect for anyone is unknown. He who speaks here
claims such a prayer: Hear me, Lord, for my cry is in earnest. I seek your statutes, to carry them out faithfully,
not merely to know them. I cried out to you; save me, and I will keep your commandments. I cried out to you; save me,
and then I will keep your commandments. Give me the salvation of the soul; by that I will do what I know ought to be done.
I came early, at an untimely hour (that is, aoria in Greek), and cried out. I hurried at an untimely hour and cried out to you. At midnight.
before the morning time came, I rose up to pray. That time is called 'in-maturitas' (untimeliness), and it is one word, not two.
One of the translators said 'in immaturitate', that is, 'en aoria' in Greek, with two prepositions. That is the same sense.
For 'inmaturitas' means 'unripe', that is, an unseasonable time, which is also commonly called 'hora inportuna' (an inconvenient hour), as midnight is, and the dead of night (intempesta),
when it is not the time for working but for resting. This saying can be understood of every one of the faithful who often does this,
who rises so early. The untimely time can also mean the time before Christ came, when the prophets cried out and begged him to come,
as he had promised. That is why it says further on: 'In your word I have hoped exceedingly.' In your promise I trusted.
That is why I cried out. If I had not longed for your coming, I would not have cried so urgently. 'My eyes have gone before you to the morning.'
My eyes went ahead of the dawn, and they kept watch ahead of it toward you. What is this dawn?
Nothing other than when day began to break for those who sat in the shadow of death, and they began to see you in the flesh. Why did I do this?
'That I might meditate on your words.' So that I might keep your promises in mind, together with all those who announced them in the Law and the Prophets.
'Hear my voice according to your mercy, O Lord; according to your judgment give me life.' Lord, hear my voice according to your
mercy, so that you grant me forgiveness in the time of mercy. According to your judgment (I mean according to the judgment of those who love your name)
quicken me to life. 'Those who persecute me have drawn near to iniquity, but they have gone far from your law.'
My persecutors drew near to injustice. In what way? Only by tormenting my flesh, because to the soul, which bears the torment,
they come no nearer. But they went far away from your law. They were near to injustice and far from justice.
'Be near, O Lord.' Lord, be near to us. Let your nearness be within us, a nearness that never forsakes us.
'And all your ways are truth.' And all your ways are truth. In that truth of your justice
you will let us suffer afflictions, because we do not suffer them without guilt. 'From the beginning I have known of your testimonies,
for you have founded them forever.' At the beginning of this world I learned from your testimonies that you established them for eternity
and gave them a foundation in Christ. This was shown in Abel, with whom the city of God, the holy Church, began; it was shown in the patriarchs and prophets
and in the others in whom the holy Church then consisted, who had the testimonies of God founded in Christ. 'Initio' (at the beginning) is an adverb, as is 'katarchas' among the Greeks.
Others said 'ab initio' (from the beginning), so that it would be more understandable [?]. 'See my humility and deliver me, for I have not forgotten your law.'
See my humility and free me, because I did not forget your law, which says to us: 'Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled,
and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.' 'Judge my judgment and redeem me.' Examine my judgment. In other words: see my
humility; see how I have judged myself. 'And redeem me' [text: 'redi me' [?]]. In other words: 'and deliver me'. 'Because of your word give me life.' Because of your promise, quicken me.
[?] they [?] me. And my heart stood in awe of your words. So it was at your words, not at their words,
that my heart was afraid. They threatened: "I proscribe you, I kill you, I torture you with hooks, I burn you with fire, I hand you over to the beasts, I tear your limbs apart."
I feared none of that, because you said: "Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul,
but fear him who has the power to destroy both body and soul in Gehenna." I will rejoice over your words like one who finds much spoil.
I rejoice in your words like someone who finds a great deal of spoil, because my victory has given me a great deal of spoil,
in those who marveled at the patience of your soldiers, turned to you, and became believers. I hated and abhorred iniquity, but I loved your law.
I hated injustice and loathed it, but I loved your law. Although I feared your words, which are your law,
I still love them, and chaste fear does not get in the way of that love. In the same way children should fear and love their parents,
and a wife should fear and love her husband. Seven times a day I have praised you for the judgments of your righteousness.
Seven times a day I praised you because of the judgments of your righteousness. "Seven times" is to be understood as "always,"
because all time is counted in periods of seven days. As it says: "The righteous man will fall seven times and rise again,"
that is, he is humbled by every kind of tribulation and makes progress. Great peace belongs to those who love your law, and nothing makes them stumble, that is, nothing offends their mind.
Those who love your law have firm peace and do not stumble. Even if someone who loves the law does not understand it,
he still believes that it has hidden and holy meanings. So he honors it and blames himself for
his lack of understanding. But the Jews stumbled when they were told to understand the law spiritually, because they did not love spiritual things.
It can also be understood this way: neither prosperity nor adversity harms those who love God's law. I waited for your salvation, O Lord,
and loved your commandments. I waited for your Savior, Christ, O Lord, and loved your commandments, the love of God and of one's neighbor.
Anyone who does not love these commandments waits for him in vain. Those who love them are now waiting for him, so that when Christ, their life, appears,
they too may appear with him in glory. My soul has kept your testimonies and loved them greatly. My soul guarded your testimonies
and loved them greatly. The martyrs say this, because if they had not kept God's commandments, martyrdom without love would have done them no good.
I have kept your commandments and your testimonies, because all my ways are in your sight. I kept your commandments and your testimonies,
because all my ways are in your sight. Since you watch over them and look on them with merciful eyes,
I keep my uprightness in them. Let my prayer come near into your presence, O Lord;
give me understanding according to your word. Let my prayer, which is before you, come near to you, Lord, as it says:
"The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart." Give me understanding according to your promise. What promise is that?
"I will give you understanding and instruct you." Let my petition come into your sight; deliver me according to your word. May my prayer come before you.
Release me according to your promise. This says the same thing again. He prays well
who prays like this. By receiving understanding he is helped, because by trying to understand on his own he comes to harm.
My lips shall pour forth a hymn when you have taught me your justifications. My lips speak a song of praise when you teach me your righteous decrees.
God teaches those who are "taught of God," so that they keep God's righteous decrees not only by remembering them but by doing them.
My tongue shall proclaim your word, for all your commandments are equity. My tongue tells your speech
and teaches your commandments, because they are all just. Therefore I want to become a minister of the word, because there is equity in it.
But I know well that dangers will meet me from those who contradict and persecute me. What will become of me then?
Let your hand be there to save me. So let your help come to keep me, so that I am not lost in my soul. For I have chosen your commandments.
For I chose your commandments, so that with love for them I overcame fear. I have longed for your salvation, O Lord, and your law is my meditation.
I wanted Christ, your Savior; I longed for him. And your law is my meditation, because the law bears witness to Christ.
My soul shall live and shall praise you, and your judgments shall help me. In him my soul lives and praises you,
and your judgments help me, together with those who are to hear: "Come, you blessed of my Father." I have gone astray like a sheep that has perished.
I went astray like a lost sheep. Seek your servant, for I have not forgotten your commandments. Seek me, seek your servant,
for I did not forget your commandments. Those whom you sought, you found. Still seek those whom you are to find and save.
A Jew who was wise in his own way was asked why the Songs of Steps were given that name. He answered like this: When David wanted to build a temple to the Lord,
he leveled the temple mount and shaped it entirely to fit the temple he wanted to build. And he dug around it in such a way
that a small hill was left on top of the mount, and he wanted to build the temple on it. On the small hill he made fifteen steps,
going around it three times, set one below another [?], so that the workmen and all the people could go up and down easily.
And because he expected that he himself would complete the work, he at once composed joyful songs for that same work,
I mean for the fifteen steps, with the same number of psalms. And the first song shows at once
that he had envious people and opponents over that same work. That is why he said: "Lord, deliver my soul from wicked lips
and from a deceitful tongue," and so on. That is the end of the Jew's account. As far as the outer bark is concerned, I believe it should not be scorned.
But if we have tasted anything sweeter from the faithful, who pressed out the marrow, and want to bring it out into the open as far as we are able,
let no one call that wish pride, for it shows no envy, which is the handmaid of pride. The Songs of the Fifteen Steps.
Thus. "Behold now, bless [the Lord], you who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house," and, as it is in the Apocalypse: "Alleluia. Amen."
"Blessing and glory and wisdom." With this comfort the Church now at last speaks to those who still dwell in Kedar.
Since it may happen to you so graciously at your end, confidently in the nights lift up all your hands in the holy places and bless the Lord.
So the nights of this last song accord with the Kedar of the first. Alleluia. Praise the name of the Lord.
"You who stand," as also above. But also, what in the fifteen divisions of the musical monochord, that is, the four tetrachords,
this very power may signify — if anyone not unlearned has examined it, the power of the Holy Spirit, who, containing all things, has knowledge of the voice —
he will find wonderful ornaments. A SONG OF ASCENTS, THAT IS, OF STEPS. TO YOU, WHEN I WAS IN TROUBLE, I CRIED,
and you heard me. I cried to you, Lord, when I was in troubles, and you heard me.
Lord, deliver my soul from unjust lips and from a deceitful tongue. Lord, free me from unjust
and deceitful words. Such are the words of those who hasten to deceive me as though they were sparing me, and who hasten to turn me aside,
so that I do not climb up from vices to virtue. "Where do you want to go?" they say. "You want to go too far,
farther than you are able." What shall be given to you, and what shall be added to you against a deceitful tongue? Then I said to myself: What will be granted to you,
and what will be set against it for you? That is, what will you have to set against such deceitful words? Sharp arrows of the mighty one,
with desolating, that is, laying-waste, coals. Sharp arrows of the mighty one do that; these are the words of God. Set them against it,
with destroying coals, that is, with the examples of those who were cold but who then kindled themselves to destroy their errors.
By doing so you climb by steps, as they also did. Woe is me, why has my sojourning been prolonged? "Ah me," you then say,
"why has my exile become so long?" Because you at once begin to long to go hence as soon as you climb up to virtue,
and the wrongdoing of others begins to weigh on you; therefore this life at once seems to you an exile and full of sorrow.
I have dwelt with the tents, that is, with the inhabitants of Kedar. I sit with those who dwell in Kedar, where the dwelling of Ishmael is,
who is to be cast out of God's kingdom. As it says: "Cast out the bondwoman and her son,
for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the free woman." His tents are Kedar, that is, darkness; in them sit sinners,
among whom I dwell here. My soul has long been a sojourner. My soul is very much in exile here.
It is weary of the tents of Ishmael. With those who hated peace I was peaceable. I kept peace with those
who hate it. These are the ones among whom I sit in Kedar, whose wickedness I endure,
so that there may still be peace between us. When I spoke to them, they fought against me without cause. Needlessly they struggled against me when I greeted them.
because I did not seek my own profit when I greeted them, but the salvation of those who are in Christ.
And because they hate peace, they could not bear to hear any mention of Christ, who is our peace.
A Song of Degrees. I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, from where help shall come to me. I looked up to the mountains.
that is, the apostles. From there help comes to me. By preaching the gospel they have shown us where the help is to come from.
My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. Help comes to me from God, who made heaven and earth. This is learned from them.
Do not let your foot be moved. Lord, do not let my foot slip through pride. Nor let him slumber who keeps Israel.
Nor let him slumber who guards you, Israel. Behold, he who keeps Israel will not slumber nor sleep. Nor does he.
He does not slumber, nor does he sleep, who guards Israel. Israel means "a man seeing God." Whoever believes in the incarnation of the Lord
is Israel, because he will come to behold the face of God. The Lord will keep you; the Lord is your covering
upon your right hand. God guards you. God is your covering and your shield over the power of your right hand,
that is, over the power of your blessedness, because you have the power to become a son of God and to be at his right hand. So he shields you,
so that you are not tempted more than you can bear. The sun shall not burn you by day, nor the moon by night. By day the sun does not harm you,
nor the moon by night. Prosperity and adversity do not harm you. The Lord keeps you from all evil; may the Lord keep your soul.
God guards you from all evil. May God guard your soul. Even if the body is slain,
may the soul be kept safe. May the Lord keep your coming in and your going out, from this time forth and for ever.
May God guard your going in when temptation begins to come upon you, so that he does not let you be too severely tested; and your going out,
so that you come out of it improved, like Job. From this time forth and for ever. May he guard you now and always.
The voice of one sighing for the Jerusalem above. I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: we shall go into the house of the Lord. I am glad of the things
that the prophets and apostles promised me. "We shall go," they said, "into God's house." That house is in heaven. Our feet were standing
in the courts of Jerusalem. Since those promises, our feet have stood in the courts of Jerusalem, because since then we have set our hope there.
Jerusalem, which is being built. That is the heavenly Jerusalem, which is being built like a city out of living and spiritual
stones. Whose participation is in the selfsame. Its participation, I mean hers: her participation is in the idipsum ("the selfsame").
She has a share in God; that is, her citizens have a share in him. He is always without change
and always one. That is why he is called idipsum ("the selfsame"), and that is why he is called est ("he is"). For there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord.
My Lord's tribes, by which I mean those who believed in him, not those who crucified him, climbed up there into the city.
he fortifies the city. For he will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the righteous. For he does not leave the power of the sinners
over the portion of the righteous. Though he lets them rule over them for a time, he does not suffer it for long.
So that the righteous may not stretch out their hands to iniquity. For he does not want the righteous, because of that distress, to stretch out their hands to injustice
and become like the wicked. Do good, O Lord, to the good and to the upright of heart. Do well, Lord, to those who have good and upright
hearts, who do not follow after the wicked. But those turning aside into [?] (transuggellationes), the Lord will lead away with those who work injustice.
Those who turn to the likeness of the [?] (iruuurgton, perhaps 'the strangled'), and learn evil from the evil, God leads away with those who act unjustly.
They go after those whom they are like. And peace upon Israel. And upon Israel comes peace, that is, rest meets him.
A SONG OF DEGREES. WHEN THE LORD TURNED THE CAPTIVITY OF ZION, we became like those comforted. When God turned the exile of Zion,
then we became as if comforted. We were made exiles by our sins, and redeemed with Christ's blood,
and we are as if comforted, because, still weeping here, we hope to ascend there,
where we shall be fully comforted. That is in the resurrection of the righteous. Then our mouth was filled with joy, and our tongue with exultation.
Then our mouth and our tongue became full of joy and gladness. The heart has its own mouth and its own tongue;
it is of these that this is spoken. Then they shall say among the nations: The Lord has done great things with us; we have been made joyful.
Then they shall say among the peoples: The Lord has done mightily with us; we have been gladdened. Because he now says in the future tense, 'they shall say,'
therefore the past tenses too, 'turned' and 'was filled', which he spoke before, are to be understood as future.
In prophecies such speech is constant. Now is the time when we should say: THE LORD HAS DONE GREAT THINGS WITH US.
For we had done evil to ourselves; then the Son of God came and did the mightiest thing for us, in that he gave himself for us.
Turn, O Lord, our captivity, like torrents in the south. When this was prophesied in words of the past tense,
it was still to come; therefore he prays that it may come to pass, thus: Turn, Lord, our exile,
as the streams are turned in the south wind. The streams are frozen in winter; when the warm wind comes,
the ice melts, and then the streams run. So we were frozen in our sins until the wind of the Holy Spirit came
and melted our sins and made us run to the fatherland. Because this must take place with tears, he promises us comfort for them too,
saying thus: Those who sow in tears shall reap in joy. Those who sow with tears reap with joy. Those who here sow alms
and good works reap when they receive eternal life as their reward. Going, they went and wept, casting their seeds.
But coming, they shall come with exultation, carrying their sheaves. They go weeping while they sow, but they come joyful with their sheaves.
...led Israel through there. Just as he now also leads his people through the bath of regeneration.
And he struck down Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea. Whereby Pharaoh died there, and his might, that is, his army.
Just as baptism now takes away sins. Who led his people through the desert. He who led his people through the wilderness.
Just as he now leads us in this barren world and helps us to salvation. Who struck down great kings.
and slew mighty kings: Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan. He who slew the powerful and mighty kings,
such as Sihon was, and Og, by whom our vices are signified, which God slays. And he gave their land as an inheritance to Israel his servant.
And he gave their land to the lineage of Abraham. For what the devil possessed, he gave to Christ, who is the seed of Abraham. For in our humility God was mindful of us.
and redeemed us from our enemies. This he did because he remembered us in our humility, and redeemed us
with his Son's blood. Who gives food to all flesh, that is, to every race of men. He who gives food to all people.
What is that? That of which Christ said: "My flesh is true food." Give thanks to the God of heaven. Praise the God of heaven.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his mercy endures forever. Praise the Lord of lords, for his mercy is eternal.
A PSALM OF DAVID AND OF JEREMIAH. By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept, when we remembered Zion.
By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion. We wept in exile when we remembered our homeland. Zi-
-on is the homeland. God bless him who longs to go there and who therefore weeps in this Babylon.
What are the rivers of Babylon? Nothing other than the fleeting joys of this world, in which those do not wish to drown
who hope to win lasting joy in Zion. They wish to stay above them, so that they are never carried downstream by wading into them.
On the willows in the midst of it we hung up our instruments. On the willows that stand in its midst
we hung our instruments. There they hang and are silent, for the willows' barrenness has silenced them.
Greedy and insolent people, who are barren trees and turn to evil whatever good is told them:
on them we are to hang up the instruments of the Scriptures. For there those who led us captive asked us for
the words of songs. And those who carried us away said: Sing us a hymn from the songs of Zion. For there they asked us,
those who had driven us into exile, what the words of the songs say. "Sing to us," they said,
"your songs; sing to us in your fashion, as at home." The demons, who entice us into sins
and have thereby driven us into exile, say this to us through wicked people, their members. To them we answer:
How shall we sing the Lord's song in a strange land? How can we sing our Lord's song in a foreign land?
Behold, Lord, you have known all things, the newest and the ancient. You know my latest things, when I became mortal, and the old things,
when I stood in sins. You formed me and laid your hand upon me. You created me, when I had sinned, for toils
in which I was not before, and you laid your hand upon me, for then you pressed me down.
Your knowledge has been made wonderful from me. Because of my guilt your knowledge has become wondrous and hard for me.
It has grown strong; I shall not be able to reach it. It is too strong for me; I cannot attain to it. But you can bring me near to it.
Where shall I go from your spirit? Where can I go before your spirit, of which the world is full? As it says: The Spirit of the Lord
will fill the whole world. And where shall I flee from your face? And where shall I flee from you? Where can I escape your wrath?
If I ascend into heaven, you are there. If I lift myself up high, there you press me back down.
If I descend into hell, you are present. If I hide myself so that I will not confess my sins, you make me confess them.
If I take my wings straight and dwell in the farthest parts of the sea, that is, of the world. If I take my wings, that is, the love of God and of neighbour,
to me in a straight course, and I dwell, that is, aim with hope at the end of this world,
which is the Day of Judgment, for there is the end of this sea of the world, in that way I escape your wrath.
For even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me. There, to that end, your hand brings me,
and your right hand holds me, so that I do not plunge into the sea before I fly across it. And I said:
Perhaps the darkness will trample me. And I said in fear: perhaps the darkness will trample me
and lead me astray. What is the darkness but this life? And the night is illumination in my delights. And therefore my night,
that is, my life, has become light in my delight, that is, Christ. He came into this night
to illuminate it. For the darkness will not be darkened by you. For by you, Christ, the darkness does not grow dark,
but by him who hides his sin and does not confess it. He doubles the darkness. And the night will be illuminated like the day.
And for the righteous man the night becomes just as light as the day; that is, adversity harms him no more than prosperity.
As its darkness, so also its light. For him prosperity and adversity go alike. For you have possessed my reins, Lord. For you
have possessed my loins; you do not allow me unchaste desires. You took me up from my mother's womb.
You have taken me out of my mother's womb. That is the perilous Babylon, whose children do not love the heavenly Jerusalem.
I will confess to you, Lord, for you have been made terribly wonderful. I confess to you, Lord, that you have become fearfully wondrous to us.
