Your works are wonderful, God, and my soul will know it exceedingly. That is because your works are wonderful, God.
The devil is their head. He is a going-around; he never sets himself onto the way. "The labor of their lips,"
that is, the lie, "shall cover them." The labor of their mouth shields them. You shield me; their lie shields them.
With it they excuse themselves of their sins. That is harder to find than the truth.
"Coals of fire shall fall upon them." Glowing coals fall upon them, for they see those kindled
who were cold before. They see that these become earnest in good deeds. "You shall cast them down." There you cast them down.
That they begrudge those others, that is what fells them. "In miseries they shall not stand." Misery befalls them; before it they cannot stand.
But the righteous do stand, for one of the righteous said: "BUT WE GLORY ALSO IN TRIBULATIONS." "A man full of tongue shall not be directed upon the earth."
A man who talks too much never gains uprightness on earth, for it says: "IN MUCH SPEAKING YOU SHALL NOT ESCAPE SIN."
Whoever is a wagging tongue is often a liar; that is great unrighteousness. "Evils shall seize the unjust man unto destruction."
Evils seize the unrighteous man unto perdition. They can also seize the good, but not unto perdition.
"I know that the Lord will do justice for the needy." I know that God does justice for those who have nothing,
"and vengeance for the poor." And he takes vengeance on behalf of the poor. "But the just shall confess to your name."
But the righteous give credit to your name, not to themselves, for everything they are able to do. To you they owe for it
thanks. "The upright shall dwell with your countenance." The upright dwell together with your face,
as it says: "WHEN HE APPEARS, WE SHALL BE LIKE HIM, FOR WE SHALL SEE HIM AS HE IS."
UNTO THE END, FOR DAVID HIMSELF. "LORD, I HAVE CRIED TO YOU; HEAR ME." Lord, says the prophet, I cried to you; hear me.
"Attend to the voice of my supplication when I cry to you." Pay heed also to my prayer when I cry to you.
As you did in the past, so do in the future: hear me always. "Let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight."
Let my prayer rise up like smoke before you; let my prayer give off a sweet scent to you. "The lifting up of my hands, an evening sacrifice."
Let the lifting up of my hands be an evening offering to you. May you have regard for my good works at my end.
"Set a guard, O Lord, on my mouth, and a door enclosing my lips." Set a guard on my mouth, Lord,
and place a door around my lips. Teach me to be careful of my words. "Do not incline my heart to words of malice,
to make excuses in sins." Do not turn my heart to ill-willed words, to excusing sins.
Teach me pure confession, which frees from death. "With men who work iniquity, and with their chosen ones, I will not share."
With the unrighteous and with their chosen ones I have no fellowship. These are the ones who deny their own sins.
Touch the mountains and they will smoke. Touch the mountains, then they will smoke. Give compunction to proud hearts;
then they will do penance. Flash forth your lightnings and you will scatter them. Flash your lightning upon them, then you will scatter them.
Terrify them with your signs, then they will give up their conspiracy. Send forth your arrows and you will throw
them into confusion. Shoot your arrows at them, then you will afflict them. Send your apostles to them, then you will make them grieve for their sins.
Send forth your hand from on high. Send, Father, your Son from heaven. He is your hand, with which you created all things.
Rescue me and deliver me from many waters. Free me from many waters, from the many that come rushing in. From the hand of foreign sons.
Free me from the hands of foreign children, who are not children of the Church. Whose mouth has spoken vanity. I mean those
whose mouth always speaks vanity. Free me from those waters. And their right hand is a right hand of iniquity. And their right hand is
the right hand of injustice. That is because they hold on the right what they ought to hold on the left; I mean earthly goods.
They ought to hold eternal goods on the right. O God, I will sing a new song to you. When Christ comes, I will sing you a new song;
that is, that I may eat his body and drink his blood. On the psaltery of ten strings I will sing to you.
On the ten-stringed psaltery I sing to you, because the ten commandments of the law are yours, and so also is the tenfold Gospel.
They have both come from you. You who give salvation to kings. You give salvation to the righteous. You who delivered David your servant
from the malicious sword, deliver me. You who freed David your servant from Goliath's malicious sword, deliver me.
My Lord's sword is well-meaning, because it separates from evil; but the devil's sword is malicious,
because it separates from good. And rescue me from the hand of foreign sons, whose mouth has spoken vanity, and their right hand
is a right hand of iniquity. This verse says the same as it said before. Whose sons are like new plantings, firmly established from their youth.
Whose sons are new, like plantings, established from youth. They are as fair as newly planted vines,
because they have firmly established new heresies in place of the old teaching of the prophets and apostles. Their daughters are adorned, decorated all around like the likeness of a temple.
Their daughters go about decked out [?]; they go adorned in the manner of a church. They have the likeness of the adornment,
not the truth. Their storehouses are full, overflowing from this into that. Their cellars are full, changing the drink
from one to another. Their sheep are fruitful, abounding in their goings-out. Their sheep are fruitful, many in their goings-out.
Many go out of their folds. Their oxen are fat. Their cows are fat. There is no ruin of the wall.
Nor does their stone wall fall. Nor any passage. Nor can anyone pass through their house. They have privacy.
Nor any clamor in their streets. Nor is there shouting in their streets. No one wakes them. They have called the people blessed who have these things.
Put not your trust in princes, in the sons of men, in whom there is no salvation. Do not trust in the powerful.
Place no confidence in the children of men, on whom your salvation does not rest. It rests only in one Son of Man,
who is also the Son of God. His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return to his earth; in that day all their thoughts shall perish.
The man's soul departs, and then the body returns again to the earth from which it came. Then all their thoughts are gone.
Death takes them away entirely. Blessed is he whose helper is the God of Jacob. Blessed is he whose helper is the Lord God of Jacob,
who made that same Jacob into Israel. His hope is in the Lord his God, who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them.
Blessed is he whose hope is in the Lord his God, not in Saturn or Neptune, but in him who made heaven and earth and sea
and all that is in them. Who keeps truth forever, and executes judgment for those who suffer wrong.
Who always guards the truth, judging on behalf of those who suffer wrong, not of those who avenge themselves. He gives food to the hungry.
He gives food to the hungry. Those who hunger for righteousness, he satisfies. The Lord raises up the crushed. He raises up those who are brought low.
Those who fall so hard that they cannot rise up, he lifts up. The Lord looses the fettered. He frees those bound with fetters.
Heavy fetters are sins and this mortality; from both of these God frees us. The Lord enlightens the blind.
He makes the ignorant wise. The Lord loves the righteous. He loves the righteous. The Lord protects the stranger. He protects the newcomer.
That is the holy Church from among the Gentiles. He will take up the orphan and the widow. Orphans and widows he receives. And the way of sinners he will destroy.
And the broad way of sinners he casts out. He turns it away from himself; therefore it leads to hell.
The Lord shall reign forever, your God, O Zion, from generation to generation. Your God, O Zion, shall reign forever.
ALLELUIA. PRAISE THE LORD, FOR A PSALM IS GOOD. That is: praise the Lord, for it is good to praise the Lord.
Praise the Lord, because his praise is good. It is good that one praises him. Psalm-singing is good.
What is that, except that one sings on the psaltery? The psaltery sounds like a lyre or a harp
or an organ. And because what one sings on it sounds aloud, therefore 'psalm' means 'high song'.
He sings a high song who praises the Highest. He praises him who lives in a praiseworthy way. Let praise be joyful and seemly to our God.
Let praise be delightful and seemly to our God. He offers him seemly praise whose ways are seemly. He sings unseemly who
acts unseemly. As it says: PRAISE IS NOT SEEMLY IN THE MOUTH OF A SINNER. The Lord, building Jerusalem,
will gather the dispersed of Israel. Building the heavenly Jerusalem, he gathers the scattered people who are called 'those who see the Lord.'
The angels see him. Those who are to see him become like the angels. These he gathers in heaven.
...hardened from ice into stone. But when he converted them, he sent them out like pieces of bread.
For he revealed many gifts of the Holy Spirit in them. "Before the face of his cold, who will endure?" Who will stand before his frost?
Those whom he lets freeze, as he did to Pharaoh. What becomes of that? "He will send out his word and will melt them." The Father sends out his Word
and melts them. As it says: "Nor is there anyone who can hide himself from his heat." The Word of the Father thaws them.
"And his spirit will blow, and the waters will flow." And his Spirit blows upon them, and after that they flow to God,
because they have been melted by his warmth. "Who declares his word to Jacob, his justices and his judgments to Israel."
He who makes known his word, that is, his command, to Jacob, and his laws and his judgments to Israel.
Those who are his faithful, they are Jacob and Israel; to them he reveals how just he is in his judgments,
how no one is saved except by grace, because they all deserved death. "He has not done so for every nation, and he has not made his judgments known to them."
He did not make himself so familiar with every people, nor did he reveal his judgments to them as he did to Israel.
Psalm of Haggai and Zechariah. Alleluia. "Praise the Lord from the heavens." These two prophets rejoice
that praise comes to God from heaven and from earth. Therefore let us say together with them: Praise God, angels, from heaven. "Praise him in the heights."
Praise him on high. "Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts." Praise him all together, both angels and hosts. "Praise him, sun and
moon; praise him, stars and light." Praise him, sun and moon, stars and daylight. "Praise him, heavens of heavens,
and let the waters that are above the heavens praise the name of the Lord." Praise him, heavens of the heavens, that is, heavens above the heavens.
And let the waters that are above heaven, which hold up the firmament, praise his name. "For he spoke, and they were made;
he commanded, and they were created." For he bade them come into being; from that they came into being. He commanded their creation;
from that they were created. "He established them for ever and for ages of ages." He has established them for ever and in eternity.
Even if heaven and earth are changed, as it says of the world to come: "There will be a new heaven and a new earth,"
they still stand forever and endure forever. "He set a decree, and it will not pass away." He set them a law that does not pass away,
because it will not be resisted by them. "Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all depths." Give him praise from the earth,
flowing waters and all immeasurably deep waters. What are the flowing waters like, if not dragons? And what waters are as deep
as the sea that encircles the earth? "Fire, hail, snow, ice, and the stormy winds that do his word."
Fire and hail and snow and ice, and stormy winds, which carry out his command. "Mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars."
Mountains and hills, fruit-bearing trees, and all cedars. "Beasts and all cattle, serpents and feathered birds."
